lessons.title: Ich möchte mich beschweren: making a complaint
lessons.goal: Make a complaint about a faulty product on the phone and in a short formal e-mail, with the five steps, key phrases, result words, lassen and polite Könnten Sie …?, and understand the shop's answers.

grammar.topic: Using what you know: a complaint (no new grammar)
grammar.point: A complaint uses grammar you know: sich beschweren über, weil with the verb at the end for the reason, deshalb/daher (verb next) or sodass (verb at the end) for the result, lassen for 'have it repaired', and Könnten Sie …? or Ich bitte Sie, … zu … for a polite wish. Formal e-mail: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, + small letter; Mit freundlichen Grüßen + name, no comma.
grammar.oneLine: Daher möchte ich das Gerät reklamieren.

mistake.wrong: Ich möchte mich über den Saugroboter beschweren, weil er ist laut.
mistake.right: Ich möchte mich über den Saugroboter beschweren, weil er laut ist.
mistake.why: Even in a long complaint sentence, weil still sends the verb to the very end.

terms.meaning: matter-of-fact: facts and a clear wish, no strong feelings or insults
the fixed first and last lines of a formal e-mail: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, … Mit freundlichen Grüßen

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Robbi ist kaputt' to a polite, clear complaint
cards.body: A new device breaks after one week. You want your money back, a repair or a new one, and you want it without a fight. Today you put everything together: sich beschweren über from A2 chapter 10, Könnten Sie …?, lassen from lesson 1 and the result words from lessons 4 and 5. No new grammar, only a strong complaint.
steps: You already know: sich beschweren über (A2 chapter 10), polite Könnten Sie …? and Ich hätte gern …, and deshalb, daher and sodass from lessons 4 and 5.
New today: the five steps of a complaint, the key phrases on the phone and in a formal e-mail, and how the shop answers.
By the end you can: complain about a faulty product on the phone and in a short e-mail, politely and clearly.

examples.de: Ich möchte mich über den Saugroboter beschweren.
examples.en: I would like to complain about the robot vacuum.
examples.why: You know this already: sich beschweren über.

examples.de: Daher möchte ich das Gerät reklamieren.
examples.en: Therefore I would like to return the faulty device.
examples.why: New today: reklamieren, the word for a faulty product.

cards.more: Think of a complaint like a recipe. You already have all the ingredients in your kitchen: polite Könnten Sie, the result words deshalb and daher, sodass, and lassen for 'have it repaired'. What you need today is the recipe: which ingredient goes in first, and how much. A good German complaint has five steps, a calm tone and a clear wish at the end. You will learn the steps, the phrases, a phone call, an e-mail and the answers of the shop, card by card.

cards.title: Five steps of a complaint
cards.body: A clear complaint has five steps, on the phone and in writing. 1. Greet and say who you are. 2. Say what you bought and when. 3. Say what is wrong. 4. Say what follows (deshalb, daher, sodass). 5. Say what you want (repair, exchange, money back) and ask politely.
cards.lead: You know the grammar pieces from earlier lessons. This first card gives you the order in which you use them, so no step gets lost.

examples.de: Ich habe am Montag einen Saugroboter bei Ihnen bestellt.
examples.en: On Monday I ordered a robot vacuum from you.
examples.why: Step 2: what and when.

examples.de: Das Gerät ist so laut, dass niemand schlafen kann.
examples.en: The device is so loud that nobody can sleep.
examples.why: Steps 3 and 4: problem and result.

examples.de: Könnten Sie das Gerät bitte reparieren lassen?
examples.en: Could you please have the device repaired?
examples.why: Step 5: a polite wish.

deeper.text: Step 2 matters more than it looks. A shop finds your order by a number: die Bestellnummer for an online order, the date and der Kassenbon (the till receipt) for a shop. Without them, the Kundenservice often cannot help, so have them ready before you call. In an e-mail, many people put the number in the subject line: Reklamation, Bestellnummer 48213.

example.de: Meine Bestellnummer ist 48213.
example.en: My order number is 48213.

cards.more: Picture a doctor's appointment. The doctor first wants to know who you are, then what is wrong, then since when. Only after that do you talk about medicine. A complaint works the same way. If you start with 'I want my money back!', the person on the phone does not know what you mean. If you start with your name, your order and the problem, they can follow you, and your wish at the end sounds fair and logical.
steps: 1. Grüßen und sich vorstellen: Guten Tag, mein Name ist Ben.
2. Was und wann: Ich habe am Montag einen Saugroboter bestellt.
3. Das Problem: Das Gerät funktioniert nicht richtig.
4. Die Folge: Der Akku ist schwach, sodass Robbi nach zehn Minuten stoppt.
5. Der Wunsch: Könnten Sie das Gerät bitte reparieren lassen?

cards.title: Key phrases: the problem and the wish
cards.body: Two groups of phrases. For the problem: Das Gerät funktioniert nicht richtig. / Es ist kaputtgegangen. / Es ist defekt. For the wish: Ich möchte es umtauschen. / Ich möchte es reparieren lassen. / Ich möchte mein Geld zurückbekommen. And the polite question: Könnten Sie mir bitte …?
cards.lead: You know the five steps. Now you get ready-made sentences for steps 3 and 5, the two moments where most learners look for words.

examples.de: Es ist nach einer Woche kaputtgegangen.
examples.en: It broke after one week.

examples.de: Ich möchte mein Geld zurückbekommen.
examples.en: I would like to get my money back.

examples.de: Könnten Sie mir bitte ein neues Gerät schicken?
examples.en: Could you please send me a new device?

deeper.text: Germans use two verbs for complaining. sich beschweren über is about anything: Ich beschwere mich über den Lärm. reklamieren is only for a product or service that is faulty, and it takes a direct object: Ich möchte den Saugroboter reklamieren. The noun is die Reklamation. In a shop you often see a sign Reklamationen next to the Kasse: that is where you bring faulty things.

example.de: Ich möchte den Saugroboter reklamieren.
example.en: I would like to make a complaint about the robot vacuum.

cards.more: Think of the phrases as a menu in a restaurant. On the left side are the problems: 'not working properly', 'broken', 'faulty'. On the right side are the dishes you can order: an exchange, a repair, your money back. You choose one from each side, then you put 'Könnten Sie bitte' in front, like saying 'I'd like … please' to the waiter. One problem plus one wish plus a polite question: that is already a complete, clear complaint.

rows: Der Akku ist nach zehn Minuten leer.
Könnten Sie mir bitte ein neues Gerät schicken?

cards.title: The phone call with the Kundenservice
cards.body: Ben calls TechnoMax. Listen to how he follows the five steps, gives his Bestellnummer and stays calm. The employee (die Mitarbeiterin) explains what happens next: Ben has to send Robbi back. Notice the result word deshalb and lassen in her answers.
cards.lead: With the steps and phrases in your toolbox, here is a whole phone call. Watch how both sides use the grammar you know.

examples.de: Ich möchte mich beschweren, weil der Saugroboter nicht richtig funktioniert.
examples.en: I would like to complain because the robot vacuum doesn't work properly.

examples.de: Deshalb müssen Sie das Gerät zurückschicken.
examples.en: That's why you have to send the device back.

examples.de: Dann lassen wir es reparieren.
examples.en: Then we will have it repaired.

deeper.text: On the phone you often first hear a machine: Drücken Sie die 1 (press 1). Then the employee says the company name and a question like Was kann ich für Sie tun?. A useful trick when you don't understand: Könnten Sie das bitte wiederholen? or Könnten Sie bitte langsamer sprechen? Nobody minds. It is much better than saying yes to something you didn't understand.

example.de: Könnten Sie das bitte wiederholen?
example.en: Could you please repeat that?

cards.more: Imagine a tennis match. The employee serves with a friendly question, Ben returns with his name and problem. She asks for a number, he gives it. She explains the rule, he asks what happens next. Nobody hits the ball too hard, and the game ends with a clear result: send Robbi back, then repair or a new device. When you call, think of this rhythm: answer, wait, answer. Short sentences are perfectly fine on the phone.
steps: Mitarbeiterin: TechnoMax Kundenservice, guten Tag. Was kann ich für Sie tun?
Ben: Guten Tag, ich möchte mich beschweren, weil der Saugroboter nicht richtig funktioniert.
Mitarbeiterin: Das tut mir leid. Haben Sie die Bestellnummer?
Ben: Ja, 48213. Robbi ist so laut, dass niemand schlafen kann, und der Akku ist nach zehn Minuten leer.
Mitarbeiterin: Das Gerät hat zwei Jahre Garantie. Deshalb müssen Sie es zurückschicken.
Ben: Und was passiert dann?
Mitarbeiterin: Wir sehen uns das Gerät an. Dann lassen wir es reparieren, oder Sie bekommen ein neues.
Ben: Gut. Könnten Sie mir das bitte per E-Mail schicken?

cards.title: The complaint e-mail
cards.body: After the call Ben writes a short e-mail. Formal frame: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, then a small letter. At the end: Mit freundlichen Grüßen, a new line, the name, with NO comma. Formal style: Sie, leider, daher, and a clear wish with a Frist (deadline).
cards.lead: On the phone, words are quickly forgotten. This card shows how Ben puts the same complaint in writing, in the formal style of a German e-mail.

examples.de: Leider ist das Gerät defekt.
examples.en: Unfortunately the device is faulty.

examples.de: Daher bitte ich Sie, das Gerät zu reparieren oder umzutauschen.
examples.en: Therefore I ask you to repair or exchange the device.

examples.de: Ich bitte um eine Antwort bis zum 20. November.
examples.en: I ask for a reply by 20 November.

deeper.text: Look at umzutauschen: with a separable verb, zu goes between the two pieces and the whole thing is written as one word: umtauschen → umzutauschen, zurückschicken → zurückzuschicken. You know zu + infinitive from B1 chapter 1. In a formal e-mail, Ich bitte Sie, … zu … is a very common and polite way to say what you want, a little more formal than Könnten Sie …?

example.de: Ich bitte Sie, mir das Geld zurückzuschicken.
example.en: I ask you to send me the money back.

cards.more: Think of the e-mail as a sandwich. The two slices of bread are fixed: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren at the top, Mit freundlichen Grüßen at the bottom. They are always the same, so you can learn them by heart. The filling is your five steps: what you bought, the problem, the result, your wish. Keep the filling short. A German Kundenservice reads many e-mails every day and is happy about clear facts, a number and a date.
steps: Betreff: Reklamation, Bestellnummer 48213
Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,

am 3. November habe ich bei Ihnen den Saugroboter „Robbi“ bestellt. Leider ist das Gerät defekt: Es ist sehr laut und stößt ständig gegen die Wände. Der Akku ist so schwach, dass Robbi nach zehn Minuten stoppt.
Das Gerät hat zwei Jahre Garantie. Daher bitte ich Sie, das Gerät zu reparieren oder umzutauschen. Ich bitte um eine Antwort bis zum 20. November.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Ben

cards.title: Polite but clear
cards.body: In Germany, complaints are usually direct and sachlich (matter-of-fact): facts, a number, a clear wish. That is not rude. Rude is a bad Ton (tone): insults, shouting, 'Sie sind schuld!'. So stay calm and friendly, but don't hide your wish. A good complaint is strong, not too strong.
cards.lead: Now you can complain on the phone and in writing. This card is about the tone: how direct Germans are, and where the line to rude is.

examples.de: Ich bin mit dem Gerät leider sehr unzufrieden.
examples.en: Unfortunately I am very dissatisfied with the device.
examples.why: Strong and polite.

examples.de: Ich erwarte eine Lösung bis Freitag.
examples.en: I expect a solution by Friday.
examples.why: Clear wish with a Frist.

examples.de: Das ist ja unglaublich!
examples.en: That's unbelievable!
examples.why: Too emotional for a complaint: keep it for friends.

deeper.text: Many Germans know their rights as customers well. For a faulty new product, a shop usually has to repair it or give you a new one first; your money back comes only if that does not work. So asking for a repair or an exchange first sounds reasonable and often works faster than demanding money at once. Mention the Garantie, and the shop knows you know the rules.

example.de: Das Gerät hat noch Garantie.
example.en: The device is still under guarantee.

cards.more: Imagine a traffic light. Green is too soft: 'Maybe, if it is not a problem, perhaps you could …' – the shop may not understand what you want. Red is too hard: 'Your product is rubbish, you are all useless!' – the person on the phone stops wanting to help. Yellow is just right: 'The device is faulty. Therefore I would like an exchange by Friday.' Germans like yellow: clear facts, a calm Ton, a fixed date.

rows: Vielleicht ist es nicht so wichtig, aber …
Ich erwarte eine Lösung bis Freitag.
Ich weiß nicht, was ich will.

cards.title: How the shop answers
cards.body: Now the other side. A shop often answers: Das tut mir leid. / Wir kümmern uns darum. / Schicken Sie uns das Gerät bitte zurück. / Wir ersetzen das Gerät (we replace it). / Sie bekommen Ihr Geld zurück. Knowing these phrases helps you understand the answer and play the employee in a role play.
cards.lead: You have been the customer on every card so far. Now you switch sides and learn what the shop says, so you understand its answer by phone or e-mail.

examples.de: Das tut mir leid. Wir kümmern uns darum.
examples.en: I'm sorry. We'll take care of it.

examples.de: Schicken Sie uns das Gerät bitte zurück.
examples.en: Please send the device back to us.

examples.de: Wir ersetzen den Akku kostenlos.
examples.en: We'll replace the battery free of charge.

deeper.text: The Umtausch (exchange) has a Frist. Many shops write in their rules that you can send a product back within 14 days without a reason. That is a deadline: after it, you need a real problem, like a defect. So when a shop writes Die Frist ist abgelaufen, it means: the deadline is over. Always check the date on your Kassenbon or order e-mail.

example.de: Die Frist für den Umtausch beträgt zwei Wochen.
example.en: The deadline for an exchange is two weeks.

cards.more: Think of a mirror. On one side you say: 'The device is broken. Could you please repair it?' On the other side the shop holds up the mirror and answers with the same words, turned around: 'I'm sorry. We'll take care of it. Please send us the device.' When you learn both sides, you understand much faster, because you already guessed what comes back. That is why many role plays in German exams let you play the customer AND the employee.

rows: they will take care of it
Schicken Sie uns das Gerät bitte zurück.

lessons.title: Der Akku des Handys: the genitive with der, die, das
lessons.goal: Say what belongs to what: parts of devices and things of people, with the genitive of der, die, das.

grammar.topic: Genitive with the definite article: des … -s/-es, der, der (plural)
grammar.point: The genitive shows whose thing or which part: der Akku des Handys. Masculine and neuter: des + noun with -s or -es. Feminine and plural: der, and the noun gets no ending. The genitive comes AFTER its noun; a name with -s comes BEFORE (Miras Handy). In speaking, von + dative often does the same job.
grammar.oneLine: Die Akkulaufzeit des Handys ist kurz.

mistake.why: das Auto is neuter: in the genitive it becomes des, and the noun gets -s.

terms.meaning: the case that shows belonging or a part of something: der Akku des Handys (the battery of the phone)
whose? The question word for the genitive: Wessen Handy ist das?
the ending of masculine and neuter nouns in the genitive: des Computers, des Hauses

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Annas Fahrrad' to 'das Fahrrad des Mannes'
cards.body: Robbi is back in the WG and everybody talks about devices: the battery of the phone, the colour of the case, the price of the model. In A2 you said Annas Fahrrad and das Handy von Mira. Today you learn the genitive with der, die, das. It is the form of e-mails, instructions, tests and the news.
steps: You already know: Annas Bild. Das ist das Handy von Mira. Wessen Handy ist das?
New today: der Akku des Handys, die Farbe der Wand, die Preise der Geräte. des + -s/-es for der and das, der for die and the plural.
By the end you can: name the parts of a device, say whose thing it is, and turn von + dative into the written genitive.

examples.de: Das ist das Handy von Mira.
examples.en: That is Mira's phone.
examples.why: You know this: von + a name, the spoken way.

examples.de: Der Akku des Handys ist leer.
examples.en: The battery of the phone is empty.
examples.why: New today: des Handys = of the phone.

cards.more: Think of a family photo with labels under each person: Annas Bruder, Leons Mutter. That was A2, and it only worked with names. Now imagine labels in a shop: der Akku des Handys, die Farbe der Hülle, die Preise der Geräte. These labels work with every noun, not only with names. The little word before the noun changes (des, der) and some nouns get an -s. That is the whole secret of today.

cards.title: Two ways to say 'of'
cards.lead: You already know von + dative for 'of'. This card puts it next to the genitive, so you see that both say the same thing in two different styles.
cards.body: German has two ways to show 'of'. In speaking, people often use von + dative: die Farbe von dem Auto. In writing (e-mails, instructions, news) the genitive is better and sounds more exact: die Farbe des Autos. With names, von is very common: das Handy von Mira. Learn both; use the genitive in written texts.

examples.de: Der Preis von dem Handy ist hoch.
examples.en: The price of the phone is high.

examples.de: Der Preis des Handys ist hoch.
examples.en: The price of the phone is high.

examples.de: Die Größe der Wohnung ist perfekt.
examples.en: The size of the flat is perfect.

deeper.text: In speaking, von dem is usually shortened to vom: der Preis vom Handy. That is fine in a chat or at the kitchen table. But in an e-mail to a shop or in a test, the genitive looks more careful. A good rule for B1: write the genitive, but do not be surprised when Germans say vom in everyday talk.

example.de: Der Akku vom Handy ist schon wieder leer.
example.en: The phone's battery is empty again already.

cards.more: Imagine two clothes for the same person. At home you wear a T-shirt: von dem Handy, vom Handy. For a job interview you wear a jacket: des Handys. The person inside is the same, only the style is different. Your German is the same too: both ways are correct and both mean 'of the phone'. Choose the T-shirt with friends in the WG and the jacket for an e-mail, a form or an exam.

cards.title: The forms: des, der, der
cards.lead: Now that you know when to use the genitive, here are its forms. There are only two articles to learn, and the noun itself changes only with der and das words.
cards.body: Masculine and neuter: des, and the noun gets -s or -es. Feminine: der, the noun stays the same. Plural: der, the noun stays the same. So feminine and plural look alike in the genitive. The noun always comes after the article, like in the other cases.

examples.de: Die Akkulaufzeit des Akkus ist kurz.
examples.en: The battery life of the battery is short.

examples.de: Die Farbe der Hülle gefällt mir.
examples.en: I like the colour of the case.

examples.de: Die Preise der Geräte sind gleich.
examples.en: The prices of the devices are the same.

deeper.text: Watch out: der now has three jobs. It is masculine nominative (der Akku), feminine dative (mit der Hülle) and feminine or plural genitive (die Farbe der Hülle). The position tells you which one it is. A der right after another noun, without a preposition, is almost always a genitive: die Marke der Kamera.

example.de: Die Marke der Kamera kenne ich nicht.
example.en: I don't know the brand of the camera.

cards.more: Picture two boxes on a table. Box one is for der and das words: put des in front and stick an -s at the end, like a little label on the back: des Akkus, des Handys. Box two is for die words and for plurals: put der in front and change nothing else: der Hülle, der Geräte. Every noun goes into one of the two boxes. If you know the gender, you know the box.

cards.title: -s or -es?
cards.lead: You saw that der and das nouns get an ending. This card shows when it is a short -s and when it is a longer -es, so you can write the right form.
cards.body: Most masculine and neuter nouns get -s: des Computers, des Fehlers, des Handys, des Akkus. Nouns that end in s, ß, x, z or sch always get -es: des Hauses, des Preises. Some short words can take both: des Fahrrads or des Fahrrades, des Lärms or des Lärmes. Feminine and plural nouns never get an ending.
steps: 1 Is the noun der or das? If die or plural: no ending (der Werbung, der Geräte).
2 Ends in s, ß, x, z, sch? Then -es: des Hauses, des Preises.
3 Ends in -er, -el, -en or a vowel? Then -s: des Computers, des Kabels, des Regens, des Handys.
4 Short word like Rad? Both are fine: des Fahrrads or des Fahrrades.

examples.de: Der Preis des Hauses ist sehr hoch.
examples.en: The price of the house is very high.

examples.de: Die Ursache des Fehlers ist klar.
examples.en: The cause of the mistake is clear.

examples.de: Das Display des Computers ist kaputt.
examples.en: The computer's display is broken.

deeper.text: Why -es after s or ß? Try to say des Hauss: two s sounds melt into one, and nobody would hear the genitive. The extra e makes a new syllable, so the ending can be heard: Hau-ses. That is also why the e appears in short words like Rad: it makes the word easier to say, but here it is optional.

example.de: Das Licht des Fahrrades ist sehr hell.
example.en: The bike's light is very bright.

cards.more: Listen to the end of the word, like a doctor listens to a heart. If the word already hisses at the end, like Haus or Preis, add -es so that the hiss gets its own little syllable: Hauses, Preises. If the word ends softly, with -er, -el, -en or a vowel, a quiet -s is enough: Computers, Kabels, Handys. When you hear nothing special, -s is the safe choice for long words.

cards.title: Owner after, name before
cards.lead: You can now build the forms. The next question is where they go in the phrase, because the genitive with an article and a name with -s stand in different places.
cards.body: The genitive with an article comes AFTER the noun it describes: die Akkulaufzeit des Handys, the battery life of the phone. A name with -s comes BEFORE the noun, with no article: Miras Handy. Never put both orders together. Rule to remember: article genitive after, name before.

examples.de: Die Akkulaufzeit des Handys ist gut.
examples.en: The phone's battery life is good.

examples.de: Miras Handy hat eine rote Hülle.
examples.en: Mira's phone has a red case.

examples.de: Leons Laptop ist schon alt.
examples.en: Leon's laptop is already old.

deeper.text: Notice the article. Miras Handy has no article, because the name already does its job: never say das Miras Handy. But in the other order the first noun keeps its article: die Kamera des Handys. English is the mirror image: 'the phone's camera' puts the owner first. German can only do that with names, so be careful when you translate.

example.de: Die Rückseite des Handys ist aus Glas.
example.en: The back of the phone is made of glass.

cards.more: Think of a train. With an article, the main noun is the engine and goes first; the genitive is a wagon hooked on behind it: die Hülle | des Handys. With a name, the name sits in front like a small sign on the engine: Miras | Handy. The engine never drives backwards. So if you have an article, hook the genitive on behind. If you have a name with -s, put it in front and drop the article.

cards.title: Wessen? Answers with the genitive
cards.lead: Knowing the order, you can now answer the question word you met in A2. Wessen? asks whose something is, and the answer can now be any person or thing, not only a name.
cards.body: Wessen? means whose? and it is followed directly by a noun: Wessen Handy ist das? In A2 you answered with a name: Das ist Bens Handy. Now you can answer with a person noun in the genitive: Das ist das Handy der Lehrerin. For things, simply name the part and its owner: der Stecker des Kabels.
steps: 1 Question: Wessen + noun + verb …? (Wessen Hülle ist das?)
2 Answer with a name: Das ist Annas Hülle.
3 Answer with a person noun: Das ist die Hülle der Lehrerin.
4 Short answer: Der Lehrerin.

examples.de: Wessen Laptop ist das?
examples.en: Whose laptop is that?

examples.de: Das ist der Laptop der Lehrerin.
examples.en: That is the teacher's laptop.

examples.de: Das ist das Zubehör der Kamera.
examples.en: Those are the camera's accessories.

deeper.text: In everyday talk many Germans avoid wessen and ask Wem gehört das? (who does this belong to?) with the dative. The answer is then dative too: Das gehört der Lehrerin. Wessen sounds a bit formal, like a police question. Both are correct; understand wessen, but use Wem gehört …? at the kitchen table.

example.de: Wem gehört die Hülle? – Der Lehrerin.
example.en: Who does the case belong to? – The teacher.

cards.more: Imagine a lost-property box in a school. The caretaker holds up a pencil case and asks: Wessen Mäppchen ist das? A child answers with a name: Das ist Leons Mäppchen. An adult might answer with a person: Das ist das Mäppchen der Lehrerin. Same question, two kinds of answer. Notice that the short answer works too: Der Lehrerin. The genitive alone is enough, like 'the teacher's' in English.

cards.title: In a tech text: Mira's new phone
cards.lead: Now you put the forms, the order and the -s rule together. Mira studies Informatik and explains her new phone in five sentences, the way a tech text does.
cards.body: Mira schreibt: „Mein neues Handy ist super. Der Bildschirm des Handys ist groß und hell. Die Kamera des Handys macht sehr gute Fotos. Die Größe des Speichers ist perfekt für meine Apps. Nur die Akkulaufzeit ist kurz: Der Akku hält nur einen Tag.“
steps: 1 der Bildschirm des Handys (neuter: des + -s)
2 die Kamera des Handys
3 die Größe des Speichers (masculine: des + -s)
4 die Akkulaufzeit: no genitive needed, it is one compound word

examples.de: Der Bildschirm des Handys ist groß und hell.
examples.en: The phone's screen is big and bright.

examples.de: Die Größe des Speichers ist perfekt.
examples.en: The size of the storage is perfect.

examples.de: Die Oberfläche des Displays ist glatt.
examples.en: The surface of the display is smooth.

deeper.text: German often has a choice: a genitive or a compound noun. die Laufzeit des Akkus and die Akkulaufzeit mean the same; the compound is shorter and very common in product texts. In a compound the last word decides the gender: der Akku + die Laufzeit = die Akkulaufzeit. If a compound exists, product texts usually prefer it.

example.de: Die Laufzeit des Akkus ist kurz.
example.en: The battery's running time is short.

cards.more: Read a product review like a map of the device. Each genitive points to one part: the screen of the phone, the camera of the phone, the size of the storage. The first noun is the part you look at; the genitive tells you which device it belongs to. When you read a test in a magazine, underline every des and der after a noun. You will quickly see how the whole text is built around one device.

drills.explanation: Der Akku des Handys ist leer.

lessons.title: Das Handy meines Bruders: genitive with ein, kein, mein
lessons.goal: Talk about the things of family and friends: the genitive of ein, kein and the possessives, names with -s, and spoken versus written style.

grammar.topic: Genitive with ein, kein and possessives; names with -s
grammar.point: ein, kein and mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, Ihr take the same endings as the article: -es for masculine and neuter (meines Bruders, eines Handys), -er for feminine and plural (meiner Schwester, keiner Geräte). The noun ending stays as in des: -s or -es for der and das words. Names take -s before the noun: Leons Fahrrad.
grammar.oneLine: Das ist das Handy meines Bruders.

mistake.why: der Bruder is masculine: the genitive is meines, and the noun gets -s. meiner is for feminine and plural.

terms.meaning: a word that says whose: mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, Ihr
the genitive endings of ein, kein and the possessives: meines (m/n), meiner (f/pl)
the style of language: spoken and relaxed, or written and careful

cards.title: Before we start: from 'des Handys' to 'meines Handys'
cards.body: In the last lesson you learned der Akku des Handys. But often the thing belongs to someone you know: my brother, a friend, our neighbour. Then you need the genitive of ein, kein and mein. Good news: the endings are the same as des and der, you only add them to the new words.
steps: You already know: der Akku des Handys, die Farbe der Hülle, Annas Fahrrad.
New today: der Akku meines Handys, die Idee einer Freundin, das Zimmer unserer Nachbarin. -es for der and das words, -er for die words and the plural.
By the end you can: say whose things they are in your family and WG, and choose between spoken and written style.

examples.de: Der Akku des Handys ist leer.
examples.en: The phone's battery is empty.
examples.why: You know this: des + -s.

examples.de: Der Akku meines Handys ist leer.
examples.en: My phone's battery is empty.
examples.why: New today: meines takes the -es of des.

cards.more: Look at the end of des: it is -es. Look at the end of der: it is -er. Now take any small word like mein, ein or unser and glue that same ending on: meines, eines, unseres; meiner, einer, unserer. It is like a colour code that moves from one word to the next. If you know which colour des or der has, you already know the colour of meines or meiner. Nothing else is new.

cards.title: ein and kein in the genitive
cards.lead: We start with the smallest new words: ein and kein. They copy the endings of des and der, and the noun ending of the last lesson stays the same.
cards.body: Masculine and neuter: eines, keines, and the noun gets -s or -es: die Idee eines Freundes, der Preis eines Handys. Feminine: einer, keiner: die Hilfe einer Nachbarin. Plural: ein has no plural; kein becomes keiner, like der. In real texts you mostly use der: die Besitzer der Geräte.

examples.de: Das ist die Idee einer Freundin.
examples.en: That is a friend's idea.

examples.de: Der Preis eines Handys ist oft hoch.
examples.en: The price of a phone is often high.

examples.de: Ich habe das Ladegerät eines Laptops gefunden.
examples.en: I found the charger of a laptop.

deeper.text: Without an article, a plural genitive is impossible to see: die Preise Geräte says nothing. German then uses von + dative even in writing: die Preise von Geräten, die Meinung von Experten. So the rule is: if there is no article to carry the -er, take von. This is not lazy spoken German, it is the correct written form.

example.de: Die Akkulaufzeit von Handys ist oft zu kurz.
example.en: The battery life of phones is often too short.

cards.more: Compare it with English: 'the idea of a friend'. In German the little word a changes its clothes: einer Freundin, eines Freundes. Think of ein as a person who copies the outfit of des and der. On a der or das day it wears -es, on a die day it wears -er. And when there are many things, ein stays at home because it has no plural, so kein or der takes its place.

cards.title: My, your, our: possessives in the genitive
cards.lead: Now the same endings move to the possessives. These are the most useful genitive words, because we talk all the time about the things of our family and friends.
cards.body: mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer and Ihr take -es for masculine and neuter, -er for feminine and plural, just like ein. The noun ending does not change: meines Bruders, ihrer Schwester, unserer Nachbarin, eures Zimmers. With unser and euer the stem stays: unseres, eures (euer loses one e).

examples.de: Das ist das Fahrrad meines Bruders.
examples.en: That is my brother's bike.

examples.de: Die Tastatur ihres Laptops ist neu.
examples.en: Her laptop's keyboard is new.

examples.de: Die Katze unserer Nachbarin ist sehr alt.
examples.en: Our neighbour's cat is very old.

deeper.text: In texts you will also meet an adjective here: der Akku des neuen Handys, die Tastatur meines alten Laptops. In the genitive the adjective after des, der, meines or meiner always ends in -en. You only need to recognise this now; you will practise adjective endings in the genitive later. Just remember: after a genitive article, -en is a safe guess.

example.de: Der Akku meines alten Laptops hält nur eine Stunde.
example.en: The battery of my old laptop lasts only one hour.

cards.more: Make your own family tree with labels. Under your brother write: das Zimmer meines Bruders. Under your sister: das Zimmer meiner Schwester. Under the people next door: der Garten unserer Nachbarin. Say each label aloud and tap the ending with your finger: -es, -er, -er. After five labels your ear knows the pattern. The trick is that you never think about 'my'; you only think about the gender of the person or thing.

cards.title: Names: Leons Fahrrad, Herrn Alis Restaurant
cards.lead: You know names with -s from A2. This card reviews them next to the new forms and adds two rules for writing names correctly.
cards.body: A name gets -s and stands BEFORE the noun, with no article: Leons Fahrrad, Annas Bilder, Frau Webers Katze. With Herr the title changes too: Herrn Alis Restaurant. German writes no apostrophe here: Annas, not Anna's. If a name already ends in s, x or z, people say it with von: das Auto von … .
steps: 1 Name + s + noun: Leons Fahrrad, Annas Bilder.
2 Frau + name + s: Frau Webers Katze.
3 Herr becomes Herrn: Herrn Alis Restaurant.
4 No apostrophe: Annas, never Anna's.
5 Name ends in s, x, z: use von + name.

examples.de: Leons Fahrrad steht im Hof.
examples.en: Leon's bike is in the courtyard.

examples.de: Annas Bilder hängen im Flur.
examples.en: Anna's pictures hang in the hallway.

examples.de: Herrn Alis Restaurant ist heute geschlossen.
examples.en: Mr Ali's restaurant is closed today.

deeper.text: You will see Anna's with an apostrophe on many shop signs, for example in names of cafés. That is English influence. The official rules allow it only to make the base form of a name clear (Andrea's Blumen, so nobody reads Andreas), so in your own texts write Annas. With names that end in s, x or z, the written form uses an apostrophe alone after the name, but in speaking almost everybody switches to von.

example.de: Frau Webers Katze schläft auf dem Sofa.
example.en: Ms Weber's cat is sleeping on the sofa.

cards.more: Think of a name tag on a suitcase. A name works like a tag that hangs on the front: Leons Koffer, Annas Koffer. The tag replaces the article, so there is no der or das. A person noun is different: it needs its own article and hangs on the back: der Koffer meines Bruders. So: names in front, everything else behind. And remember the German tag has no little apostrophe hook, only the plain -s.

cards.title: Genitive chains: one step at a time
cards.lead: You can now name an owner with a name, an article or a possessive. This card shows what happens when the owner itself has an owner, and how to keep it simple.
cards.body: Sometimes the owner has an owner: die Freundin meines Bruders, the girlfriend of my brother. Build it from left to right: first the main noun, then the genitive. One genitive per sentence is clear and natural. Two in a row are possible in written German, but they quickly become hard to read.
steps: 1 Main noun: die Freundin
2 Whose? my brother → meines Bruders
3 Together: die Freundin meines Bruders
4 Keep it at one genitive when you speak.

examples.de: Die Freundin meines Bruders studiert Informatik.
examples.en: My brother's girlfriend studies computer science.

examples.de: Das Passwort des Computers kennt nur Mira.
examples.en: Only Mira knows the computer's password.

examples.de: Die Besitzerin des Fahrrads wohnt im dritten Stock.
examples.en: The owner of the bike lives on the third floor.

deeper.text: In official texts you meet two genitives in a row: das Auto der Freundin meines Bruders. Read it backwards: my brother, his girlfriend, her car. It is correct, but it is heavy. In speaking, Germans break the chain with a name or a new sentence: Sie ist die Freundin von meinem Bruder. Ihr Auto ist rot. For a test, one genitive is enough.

example.de: Das Auto der Freundin meines Bruders ist rot.
example.en: My brother's girlfriend's car is red.

cards.more: Imagine Russian dolls, one inside the other. The big doll is the thing you talk about: die Freundin. Open it, and inside is the owner: meines Bruders. You could open that doll too and find another owner, but after two dolls nobody can follow any more. In real conversations Germans stop after one doll and start a new sentence. Do the same: one genitive, then a full stop, then the next idea.

cards.title: Spoken or written? Choose the style
cards.lead: Now you know all the genitive forms for people. But do Germans really say them at home? This card shows which style fits which situation.
cards.body: At home and with friends, most people say von + dative: das Auto von meinem Bruder. In e-mails, letters, the news, instructions and exams, the genitive is normal: das Auto meines Bruders. Both are correct German. A B1 learner should understand both and write the genitive in formal texts.

examples.de: Das ist das Auto von meinem Bruder.
examples.en: That is my brother's car.

examples.de: Das ist das Auto meines Bruders.
examples.en: That is my brother's car.

examples.de: Ich schicke Ihnen die Nummer meiner Bestellung.
examples.en: I am sending you the number of my order.

deeper.text: Some Germans joke that the genitive is dying, and there is a famous book title about the dative eating the genitive. In daily talk this is partly true. But in writing the genitive is alive: news, contracts, school texts and e-mails to companies use it all the time. If you use it in a complaint e-mail, you sound careful and serious.

example.de: Die Reparatur meines Computers hat zu lange gedauert.
example.en: The repair of my computer took too long.

cards.more: Picture two microphones. One is the small microphone of your phone when you send a voice message to a friend: von meinem Bruder, from my brother, easy and fast. The other is the big microphone on a stage or in a TV studio: meines Bruders, short and clear. Before you speak or write, ask yourself which microphone is in front of you. Then choose the style that fits it.

cards.title: Wessen Handy ist das? A WG dialogue
cards.lead: Now everything comes together in a short scene. Leon finds a phone in the WG kitchen and asks around. Listen for names with -s and possessives in the genitive.
cards.body:
Leon: Wessen Handy ist das? Es lag auf dem Tisch.
Anna: Ist das nicht das Handy deiner Schwester? Sie war gestern hier.
Leon: Nein, die Hülle meiner Schwester ist blau.
Mira: Das ist Bens Handy. Ich kenne die Hülle.
Ben: Ach, danke! Ich habe es aus Versehen liegen lassen.
Leon: Und das Ladegerät? Ist das auch deins?
steps: 1 Wessen Handy ist das? (question)
2 das Handy deiner Schwester (feminine: deiner)
3 die Hülle meiner Schwester (feminine: meiner)
4 Bens Handy (name + s, in front)

examples.de: Ist das nicht das Handy deiner Schwester?
examples.en: Isn't that your sister's phone?

examples.de: Die Hülle meiner Schwester ist blau.
examples.en: My sister's case is blue.

examples.de: Das ist Bens Handy.
examples.en: That is Ben's phone.

deeper.text: Look at Leon's last question: Ist das auch deins? deins means yours, a possessive standing alone without a noun. It takes the ending of the missing noun: das Ladegerät → deins, der Laptop → deiner, die Hülle → deine. Germans use these short forms all the time in speaking instead of repeating the noun.

example.de: Ist das Ladegerät deins? – Nein, meins ist schwarz.
example.en: Is the charger yours? – No, mine is black.

cards.more: Read the dialogue like a detective story with one clue in each line. Clue one: the phone was on the table. Clue two: Leon's sister was there yesterday. Clue three: the case of his sister is blue, so it is not hers. Clue four: Mira knows the case. Every clue that names an owner uses a genitive or a name with -s. When you can find all four owners, you have understood the lesson.

drills.prompt: Das ist das Zimmer ___ Bruders.
drills.hint: der Bruder is masculine.
drills.explanation: das Zimmer meines Bruders: masculine = -es.

drills.prompt: Die Katze ___ Nachbarin ist krank.
drills.hint: die Nachbarin is feminine.
drills.explanation: Die Katze unserer Nachbarin ist krank.

drills.prompt: Das Ladegerät ___ ist weg. (ihr Handy)
drills.hint: das Handy: the possessive takes -es, the noun -s.
drills.explanation: Das Ladegerät ihres Handys ist weg.

drills.prompt: Das ist die Idee ___. (eine Freundin)
drills.hint: Feminine: which ending for ein?
drills.explanation: Das ist die Idee einer Freundin.

drills.prompt: Mira's bike: which is correct written German?
drills.hint: No apostrophe, no article.
drills.explanation: Miras Fahrrad

drills.prompt: Written style: das Auto von meinem Bruder → das Auto ___
drills.hint: Masculine possessive genitive + -s on the noun.
drills.explanation: das Auto meines Bruders

blind.prompt: Write in German: The keyboard of my laptop is broken.
answers: Die Tastatur meines Laptops ist kaputt.
Die Tastatur meines Laptops ist kaputt
blind.hint: der Laptop: possessive with -es, noun with -s.
blind.explanation: Die Tastatur meines Laptops ist kaputt.

check.prompt: Der Bildschirm ___ Computers ist zu klein.
check.hint: der Computer is masculine.
check.explanation: Der Bildschirm seines Computers ist zu klein.

check.prompt: Die Wohnung ___ ist sehr hell. (meine Eltern)
check.hint: Plural: the same ending as feminine.
check.explanation: Die Wohnung meiner Eltern ist sehr hell.

check.prompt: Which phrase is correct?
check.hint: Herr changes, and the name stands in front.

lessons.title: Das Repair-Café: new technology and repairing together
lessons.goal: Understand information about a new technology and talk about the Repair-Café, using the genitive and relative clauses you know.

grammar.topic: Using the genitive and relative clauses in information texts (no new grammar)
grammar.point: No new grammar today: you use what you know. Information texts are full of genitives (die Idee des Repair-Cafés, die Reparatur der Geräte), and relative clauses explain new things (Ein Sensor ist ein kleines Gerät, das merkt, wann jemand kommt). Watch the gender: das Café → des Cafés.
grammar.oneLine: Die Idee des Repair-Cafés ist einfach: Man repariert zusammen.

mistake.why: das Café is neuter, so the genitive is des, and the noun gets -s: des Repair-Cafés.

terms.meaning: a meeting where volunteers help people repair their broken things for free
a home where devices are connected and controlled by an app
a reading strategy: look for was? wie? wo? and the Vorteil and Nachteil

cards.title: Before we start: from 'kaputt' to 'Wir reparieren das zusammen'
cards.body: Robbi is still broken, and the WG talks about technology. Mira, who studies Informatik, explains her Smart Home. Then Frau Weber has news: her club „Viertel hilft“ opens a Repair-Café. Today there is no new grammar. You read and talk about technology with the genitive and relative clauses you already know.
steps: You already know: Robbi ist kaputt. Der Akku des Handys ist leer. Ben lässt Robbi reparieren.
New today: das Smart Home, der Sensor, das Repair-Café, die Spende, ehrenamtlich helfen, nicht wegwerfen.
By the end you can: understand a short text about a new technology, explain a device with a relative clause, and invite someone to the Repair-Café.

examples.de: Robbi ist kaputt.
examples.en: Robbi is broken.
examples.why: You know this: a simple sentence.

examples.de: Im Repair-Café reparieren wir das zusammen.
examples.en: At the repair café we repair it together.
examples.why: New today: a place where people repair together.

cards.more: Think about the last thing that broke in your home: a lamp, a cable, a pair of trousers. Did you throw it away or try to fix it? Today is about that choice. First you meet new technology that makes life easier, then a place where people save old things from the bin. The grammar is your old toolbox: genitives to name the parts, relative clauses to explain what a thing does.

cards.title: Mira's Smart Home
cards.lead: We start at the WG table. Mira studies Informatik and explains how a Smart Home works. She uses relative clauses, which you know from A2, to explain new words.
cards.body: Mira erklärt: „Ein Sensor ist ein kleines Gerät, das merkt, wann jemand ins Zimmer kommt. Dann schaltet die App das Licht ein. Die Heizung geht aus, wenn niemand zu Hause ist. Das ist ja praktisch!“ A relative clause after a noun is the easiest way to explain a new thing.
steps: 1 Der Sensor merkt: jemand kommt ins Zimmer.
2 Die App bekommt die Information.
3 Die App schaltet das Licht ein.
4 Niemand ist zu Hause: Die Heizung geht aus.

examples.de: Ein Sensor ist ein Gerät, das merkt, wann jemand kommt.
examples.en: A sensor is a device that notices when someone comes.

examples.de: Die App schaltet das Licht ein.
examples.en: The app switches the light on.

examples.de: Ein Smart Home ist eine Wohnung, die man mit einer App steuert.
examples.en: A smart home is a flat that you control with an app.

deeper.text: Germany is known for a strong interest in privacy (Datenschutz). Many Germans like smart devices but ask: Who can see my data? A sensor that knows when you are at home also knows when you are away. So in German tech texts you often read about Datenschutz next to the Vorteile. When you read about a new device, look for this point too.

example.de: Der Datenschutz des Systems ist sehr wichtig.
example.en: The data protection of the system is very important.

cards.more: Imagine you have to explain a new thing to your grandmother, who has never seen it. You do not need a long definition. You take a word she knows and add a relative clause: a sensor is a small device that notices people. An app is a little program that you open on the phone. That is the trick of every good explainer: known word, then der, die or das, then what it does.

cards.title: Reading about new technology: the W-questions
cards.lead: You have heard Mira explain one device. Now you read a short information text alone. A simple strategy helps you find the important facts quickly, even with unknown words.
cards.body: When you read about a new technology, look for four answers: Was ist das? Wie funktioniert es? Was ist der Vorteil? Was ist der Nachteil? Read the text once only for these answers. Underline the genitives too: they show which part or which person the text is talking about.
steps: 1 Was ist das? (the name and a short explanation)
2 Wie funktioniert es? (the steps)
3 Was ist der Vorteil? (why it is good)
4 Was ist der Nachteil? (the problem)

examples.de: Ein Saugroboter ist ein Gerät, das allein sauber macht.
examples.en: A robot vacuum is a device that cleans by itself.

examples.de: Der Vorteil des Geräts ist klar: Man spart Zeit.
examples.en: The advantage of the device is clear: you save time.

examples.de: Ein Nachteil ist die kurze Akkulaufzeit.
examples.en: A disadvantage is the short battery life.

deeper.text: Information texts like to put the genitive at the very start: Die Akkulaufzeit des Geräts beträgt zwei Stunden. The verb betragen (to amount to) is typical of product texts and you will meet it in tests. You can say the same simply: Der Akku hält zwei Stunden. Recognise the formal verb, but use the simple one when you speak.

example.de: Die Akkulaufzeit des Geräts beträgt zwei Stunden.
example.en: The device's battery life is two hours.

cards.more: Treat the text like a newspaper photo with four people in it. You only want to know the four main people, not everyone in the background. Was, wie, Vorteil, Nachteil: those are your four people. When you have found them, stop and write them down in four short lines. Unknown words in the background are not important. With this habit a long text becomes a small card with four answers.

cards.title: Culture: the Repair-Café
cards.lead: One answer to broken devices is not technology but people. This card explains the Repair-Café, a place you find in many German cities and villages.
cards.body: In a Repair-Café, people bring broken things: lamps, toasters, bikes, clothes. Volunteers (Freiwillige) help them to repair the things together. The help is free; many people give a small Spende. The idea comes from the Netherlands, and today many cities in Germany have one. The aim is simple: repair instead of throwing away.

rows: nichts; man kann eine Spende geben
weniger Müll, gut für die Umwelt

examples.de: Die Idee kommt aus den Niederlanden.
examples.en: The idea comes from the Netherlands.

examples.de: Die Freiwilligen arbeiten ehrenamtlich.
examples.en: The volunteers work without pay.

examples.de: Die Idee des Repair-Cafés ist gut für die Umwelt.
examples.en: The idea of the repair café is good for the environment.

deeper.text: In a Repair-Café you do not just leave your toaster and come back later. You sit next to the volunteer and repair it together. The idea is that you learn something, so next time you can do it yourself. Germans often use the word nachhaltig (sustainable) for this: things last longer, and fewer things go into the bin.

example.de: Reparieren ist nachhaltig, denn man wirft weniger weg.
example.en: Repairing is sustainable, because you throw away less.

cards.more: Picture a kitchen table in a community hall with tools, coffee and cake. A retired electrician sits there with a teenager and a broken lamp. Nobody gets money, nobody is a customer. People talk, laugh and learn. That is the feeling of a Repair-Café: half workshop, half neighbourhood party. It is not a shop with a service, it is a place where neighbours help each other and keep things out of the bin.

cards.title: „Viertel hilft“ opens a Repair-Café
cards.lead: Now you know what a Repair-Café is. Frau Weber's neighbourhood club makes a poster for its own one. Read it with the W-questions and find the key information.
cards.body: Repair-Café im Viertel! Jeden ersten Samstag im Monat, von 14 bis 17 Uhr, im Gemeindehaus. Bringen Sie Ihre kaputten Geräte mit: Lampen, Toaster, Fahrräder, Kleidung. Unsere Freiwilligen reparieren mit Ihnen zusammen. Die Reparatur kostet nichts, wir freuen uns aber über eine Spende. Es gibt Kaffee und Kuchen. Ihr Verein „Viertel hilft“
steps: 1 Wann? jeden ersten Samstag im Monat, 14 bis 17 Uhr
2 Wo? im Gemeindehaus
3 Was? kaputte Geräte, Fahrräder, Kleidung
4 Kosten? nichts, aber eine Spende ist willkommen

examples.de: Das Repair-Café ist jeden ersten Samstag im Monat.
examples.en: The repair café is every first Saturday of the month.

examples.de: Wir treffen uns im Gemeindehaus.
examples.en: We meet in the community hall.

examples.de: Wir freuen uns über eine Spende.
examples.en: We are happy about a donation.

deeper.text: Look at jeden ersten Samstag im Monat. Without a preposition, a time phrase like this is in the accusative: jeden Samstag, jeden Morgen, nächsten Montag. Many German posters use exactly this form. The polite request Bringen Sie … mit! is the Sie imperative you know, and Wir freuen uns über … is the friendly German way to ask for money without asking directly.

example.de: Wir öffnen jeden ersten Samstag im Monat.
example.en: We open every first Saturday of the month.

cards.more: A poster is like a phone message from a busy friend: short, no long sentences, only the facts. When you read it, ask the questions a friend would ask before going: When? Where? What do I bring? What does it cost? If you can answer all four after one reading, the poster did its job. Try it now: cover the text and answer the four questions from memory.

cards.title: What can you bring? Device, problem, solution
cards.lead: The poster lists many things you can bring. This card puts them in a table with the typical problem and what the volunteers do, so you can describe your own broken thing.
cards.body: To get help, say three things: what it is, what the problem is, and what you want. Das ist mein Toaster. Er wird nicht mehr warm. Können Sie mir helfen? Use the genitive for the broken part: Der Stecker des Kabels ist kaputt.

examples.de: Das ist mein Toaster. Er wird nicht mehr warm.
examples.en: This is my toaster. It doesn't get warm any more.

examples.de: Der Schalter der Lampe funktioniert nicht.
examples.en: The lamp's switch doesn't work.

examples.de: Können Sie mir einen Knopf an die Hose nähen?
examples.en: Can you sew a button onto my trousers for me?

deeper.text: For the problem, German likes er, sie, es for the device, matching its gender: der Toaster → er, die Lampe → sie, das Fahrrad → es. English always says it. So: Mein Toaster? Er geht nicht. Not: Es geht nicht. If you say es for a masculine thing, people understand you, but it sounds like a beginner. Match the pronoun to der, die, das.

example.de: Die Lampe? Sie geht nicht mehr an.
example.en: The lamp? It doesn't switch on any more.

cards.more: Think of the help desk at a doctor's practice. You say who the patient is, where it hurts and what you hope for. A broken device is your patient. Das ist mein Wasserkocher: the patient. Der Stecker ist kaputt: where it hurts. Können Sie mir helfen?: what you hope for. Three short sentences, and the volunteer knows exactly what to do. Practise it with one broken thing from your own home.

cards.title: In the Repair-Café: Robbi gets help
cards.lead: Now you see the Repair-Café in action. Ben finally brings Robbi, his robot vacuum. Frau Weber welcomes him, and Leon, who helps there, opens the casing.
cards.body:
Frau Weber: Willkommen! Was haben Sie mitgebracht?
Ben: Das ist Robbi, mein Saugroboter. Er fährt nicht mehr.
Leon: Ich öffne das Gehäuse.
Frau Weber: Leon hilft hier ehrenamtlich.
Leon: Hier ist das Problem: Das Kabel des Akkus war locker.
Ben: Kannst du das reparieren?
Leon: Klar, das reparieren wir gleich.
Frau Weber: Das kostet nichts. Eine Spende ist willkommen.
steps: 1 Ben bringt Robbi ins Repair-Café.
2 Leon öffnet das Gehäuse.
3 Das Problem: Das Kabel des Akkus war locker.
4 Die Reparatur kostet nichts, eine Spende ist willkommen.

examples.de: Das Kabel des Akkus war locker.
examples.en: The battery cable was loose.

examples.de: Ich öffne das Gehäuse.
examples.en: I'm opening the casing.

examples.de: Das reparieren wir gleich.
examples.en: We'll repair that right away.

deeper.text: Notice Das reparieren wir gleich. The object das stands in position 1, not the subject. Germans do this to connect to what was just said: the problem → das. The verb stays in position 2, and wir moves behind it. In speaking this sounds natural and friendly. In English you would say: We'll fix that right away.

example.de: Den Stecker tauschen wir auch gleich.
example.en: We'll swap the plug straight away too.

cards.more: Read the scene like a short film in three shots. Shot one: the welcome at the door and Robbi in Ben's hands. Shot two: Leon with the screwdriver, the open casing and the loose cable. Shot three: a happy Ben and the question of money. In each shot one sentence carries the story: Er fährt nicht mehr; das Kabel des Akkus war locker; die Reparatur kostet nichts. Find these three, and you know the whole scene.

lessons.title: Wegen des Regens: wegen + genitive
lessons.goal: Give a reason with a noun instead of a clause: wegen + genitive, turn weil-clauses into wegen-phrases, and know the spoken dative form.

grammar.point: wegen means 'because of' and takes the genitive: des + noun (-s/-es) for masculine and neuter, der for feminine and plural, eines/einer with ein. A weil-clause becomes a wegen-phrase: weil es regnet → wegen des Regens. In position 1 the verb follows straight after the phrase. In speech many people use the dative (wegen dem Regen); in writing use the genitive.
grammar.oneLine: Wegen des Regens kommen nur wenige Leute.

mistake.wrong: Wegen dem Regen ist das Fest ausgefallen. (in a written text)
mistake.right: Wegen des Regens ist das Fest ausgefallen.
mistake.why: wegen dem Regen is everyday spoken German. In emails, comments and exams use the written standard: wegen + genitive, des Regens.

terms.meaning: 'because of' + des/der: gives a reason as a noun
the form for emails, comments and exams; speech is often more relaxed
'fine by me' (recognise only)

cards.title: Before we start: from 'weil es regnet' to 'wegen des Regens'
cards.body: It is Saturday, it is raining, and the new Repair-Café in the Gemeindehaus is half empty. Why? You can already say it with a whole clause: weil es regnet. Today you learn the short way that German uses in news, notices and quick answers: one little word, wegen, plus a noun in the genitive.
steps: You already know: weil and da with the verb at the end (B1 chapter 1) and the genitive des/der from Miras Handy and der Name des Cafés.
New today: wegen + genitive gives the reason as a noun: wegen des Regens, wegen der Kosten.
By the end you can: turn a weil-clause into a wegen-phrase and explain why the Repair-Café is so quiet.

examples.de: Es kommen nur wenige Leute, weil es regnet.
examples.en: Only a few people are coming because it is raining.
examples.why: You know this already: weil, verb at the end.

examples.de: Wegen des Regens kommen nur wenige Leute.
examples.en: Because of the rain only a few people are coming.
examples.why: New today: the same reason, now as a noun.

cards.more: Think of a reason as a suitcase. With weil you pack a whole sentence into it: a subject, a verb at the end, everything. With wegen you pack only one thing: a noun. Wegen des Regens. Wegen der Kosten. The suitcase is smaller, so the sentence gets shorter and sounds more like a news report or a sign on a door. You will meet this short form everywhere in Germany, from train stations to shop windows. Today we pack the small suitcase, step by step.

cards.title: wegen + genitive: the reason as a noun
cards.body: wegen means 'because of'. It takes the genitive. Masculine and neuter: des, and the noun gets -s or -es (des Regens, des Wetters, des Preises). Feminine and plural: der, no ending (der Hitze, der Kosten). With ein: eines Fehlers, einer Baustelle.
cards.lead: You know the genitive from Miras Handy. This card puts it to work: after the little word wegen, the reason noun always stands in the genitive.

examples.de: Wegen des Regens bleiben wir drinnen.
examples.en: Because of the rain we stay inside.

examples.de: Wegen der Kosten repariert Ben Robbi selbst.
examples.en: Because of the costs Ben repairs Robbi himself.

examples.de: Wegen eines Fehlers funktioniert der Toaster nicht.
examples.en: Because of a fault the toaster doesn't work.

deeper.text: The word deswegen, which you met as 'that's why', is just des + wegen glued together: 'because of that'. The same glue makes meinetwegen, literally 'because of me'. In real life it means 'fine by me, I don't mind': Kann ich das Fenster aufmachen? – Meinetwegen! You only need to recognise meinetwegen; it often sounds a little bored or reluctant.

example.de: Kann ich das Fenster aufmachen? – Meinetwegen!
example.en: Can I open the window? – Fine by me!

cards.more: Imagine wegen as a magnet for the genitive. Whatever noun comes near it changes its clothes: der Regen becomes des Regens, die Hitze becomes der Hitze. In English nothing changes after 'because of', so this feels strange at first. A trick: for der and das words, listen for the little -s at the end, like the English 's in 'the rain's fault'. For die words and plurals, simply say der. Two patterns, that is all: des …s, or der.

cards.title: From weil to wegen: clause into noun
cards.body: Three steps turn a weil-clause into a wegen-phrase. Find the noun that carries the reason (es regnet → der Regen). Take its article. Put it in the genitive. Sometimes the noun comes from an adjective: weil es laut ist → wegen des Lärms; weil es heiß ist → wegen der Hitze.
cards.lead: Now that you know the genitive forms after wegen, this card shows how to get there from a weil-clause you can already build.

examples.de: Weil es laut ist, kann Leon nicht lernen.
examples.en: Because it is loud, Leon can't study.

examples.de: Wegen des Lärms kann Leon nicht lernen.
examples.en: Because of the noise Leon can't study.

examples.de: Wegen der Hitze öffnet das Café erst um fünf.
examples.en: Because of the heat the café only opens at five.

steps: Find the thing that carries the reason: es regnet → der Regen.
Take its article: der.
Make it genitive after wegen: wegen des Regens.

deeper.text: Not every weil-clause has an easy noun. Weil ich müde bin, weil Mira keine Lust hat: here German speakers keep weil, because a noun version would sound stiff. Use wegen when there is a clear thing to blame, often weather, money, noise, traffic or a problem. Use weil for feelings and personal reasons. Both are correct; good German simply picks the shorter, more natural one.

example.de: Mira bleibt zu Hause, weil sie müde ist.
example.en: Mira stays at home because she is tired.

cards.more: Picture a newspaper headline. A reporter has very little space, so 'Because it is raining very hard, the market is cancelled' becomes 'Market cancelled because of heavy rain'. German does the same: weil es stark regnet becomes wegen des Regens. You throw away the verb and keep the one noun that holds the whole reason. Ask yourself: which thing is to blame? The rain, the noise, the price, the heat. That thing, in the genitive, goes after wegen.

cards.title: Where the wegen-phrase stands
cards.body: The whole wegen-phrase is one block. In position 1 the verb comes right after it, then the subject: Wegen des Regens bleiben wir drinnen. It can also stand in the middle, after the verb and subject: Wir bleiben wegen des Regens drinnen. A second verb part stays at the end.
cards.lead: You can build the wegen-phrase now. This card shows where it goes in the sentence, at the start or in the middle, and what the verb does.

examples.de: Wegen des Sturms ist das Fest ausgefallen.
examples.en: Because of the storm the party was cancelled.

examples.de: Das Fest ist wegen des Sturms ausgefallen.
examples.en: The party was cancelled because of the storm.

examples.de: Wir müssen wegen des Streiks mit dem Rad fahren.
examples.en: We have to go by bike because of the strike.

deeper.text: In very formal texts, wegen can stand after its noun: des Wetters wegen. You will see this in old books or official letters, almost never in speech. You only need to recognise it. A related word you already use, deswegen, shows the same old order: des + wegen. So the 'back to front' wegen is not a mistake, just old-fashioned style.

example.de: Des Wetters wegen bleibt das Museum geschlossen.
example.en: Because of the weather the museum stays closed.

cards.more: Think of the wegen-phrase as one heavy box that you can carry to two places. Put it at the front door, position 1, and the verb must stand right behind it, like a guard: Wegen des Sturms ist … Put it in the living room, the middle of the sentence, and everything else keeps its usual place. The box never breaks apart: wegen and its noun always travel together. Only the verb's second part waits at the very end, as always.

cards.title: Ein Regentag im Repair-Café
cards.body: Read the mini text. Find the four wegen-phrases and say which thing is to blame each time. Notice: two are at the start, two in the middle.
cards.lead: You know where the wegen-phrase goes. Now read it in a real scene: a rainy Saturday at Frau Weber's Repair-Café, with four reasons in a row.

examples.de: Wegen des Regens kommen heute nur wenige Leute.
examples.en: Because of the rain only a few people are coming today.

examples.de: Herr Ali kommt wegen einer Baustelle zu spät.
examples.en: Herr Ali is late because of a building site.

examples.de: Wegen des Stromausfalls funktioniert der Wasserkocher nicht.
examples.en: Because of the power cut the kettle doesn't work.

examples.de: Leon arbeitet wegen der Kälte mit Handschuhen.
examples.en: Leon works with gloves because of the cold.

steps: Wegen des Regens kommen heute nur wenige Leute.
Herr Ali kommt wegen einer Baustelle zu spät.
Wegen des Stromausfalls funktioniert der Wasserkocher nicht.
Leon arbeitet wegen der Kälte mit Handschuhen.
Aber die Stimmung ist gut, und alle trinken Tee aus der Thermoskanne.

deeper.text: Repair-Cafés started in the Netherlands, and today you find them in many German towns, often in a Gemeindehaus or a library. Volunteers repair things for free; people give a Spende if they want. Germans also write wegen on notices there: 'Wegen Krankheit geschlossen' (closed due to illness). On signs the article often disappears completely, so the genitive is invisible.

example.de: Heute wegen Krankheit geschlossen.
example.en: Closed today due to illness.

cards.more: Imagine you are the reporter for the Kiez newsletter, standing in the wet doorway with a notebook. You don't write long weil-sentences; you write what went wrong, quickly: rain, a building site, a power cut, the cold. Each one becomes a tiny wegen-phrase. Read the four lines aloud and point at the guilty thing in each: der Regen, eine Baustelle, der Stromausfall, die Kälte. If you can name the guilty thing and its genitive article, you have understood the whole lesson.

cards.title: Spoken German: wegen dem Regen
cards.body: In everyday speech many Germans say wegen dem Regen, with the dative. You will hear it at the bakery and on the bus. In writing (emails, comments, exams) use the genitive: wegen des Regens. In this course the tests always ask for the genitive, the written standard.
cards.lead: You have now read wegen in a text. This card is about what you will actually hear on the street, and why it differs from what you write.

examples.de: Wegen dem Regen bleib ich heute zu Hause.
examples.en: Because of the rain I'm staying home today. (spoken)

examples.de: Wegen des Regens bleibe ich heute zu Hause.
examples.en: Because of the rain I'm staying home today. (written)

examples.de: Wegen der Verspätung schreibe ich eine E-Mail.
examples.en: Because of the delay I'm writing an email.

deeper.text: Careful with feminine and plural nouns: wegen der Hitze is genitive, but it would also be the dative form of die Hitze. So here spoken and written German sound the same. The difference only shows with masculine and neuter words: des Regens (written) against dem Regen (spoken). Another spoken shortcut: wegen mir instead of meinetwegen, meaning 'because of me'.

example.de: Das Café schließt wegen der Hitze früher.
example.en: The café closes earlier because of the heat.

cards.more: Think of clothes. At home you wear a T-shirt; to a job interview you wear a shirt. Both are real clothes, both are fine in their place. Wegen dem Regen is the T-shirt: relaxed, everyday, heard in every city. Wegen des Regens is the shirt: what you put in an email to your landlord, a forum comment or the Goethe exam. Your ear should accept both. Your pen should choose the genitive. With feminine and plural nouns you won't even notice: der works in both.

cards.title: Warum ist es heute so leer?
cards.body: Mira helps at the Repair-Café. She asks Frau Weber why so few people came. Listen to the short answers: a wegen-phrase alone can be a full answer to Warum?
cards.lead: You know spoken and written wegen. Now hear it in a short conversation between Mira and Frau Weber, where single wegen-phrases answer the question Warum?

examples.de: Warum ist es heute so leer?
examples.en: Why is it so empty today?

examples.de: Wegen des Wetters, glaube ich.
examples.en: Because of the weather, I think.

examples.de: Und wegen des Streiks. Die Busse fahren nicht.
examples.en: And because of the strike. The buses aren't running.

steps: Mira: Frau Weber, warum ist es heute so leer?
Frau Weber: Wegen des Wetters, glaube ich. Und wegen des Streiks.
Mira: Ach ja, die Busse fahren nicht.
Frau Weber: Genau. Wegen der Kälte bleiben viele Leute lieber zu Hause.
Mira: Dann haben wir mehr Zeit für Robbi!
Frau Weber: Ha, genau! Komm, wir fangen an.

deeper.text: A short wegen-answer is perfect in speech, but in writing it counts as an incomplete sentence. In an email write the whole thing: Es sind nur wenige Leute gekommen, wegen des Wetters. Also notice the little word glaube ich at the end: it softens the answer and shows you are guessing. Germans add it all the time to sound less sure and more polite.

example.de: Wegen des Wetters sind nur wenige Leute gekommen.
example.en: Because of the weather only a few people came.

cards.more: Picture yourself at a bus stop. Someone asks you, 'Why isn't the bus coming?' You don't answer with a long sentence. You say, 'Because of the strike.' German works the same way: Wegen des Streiks. This is one of the nicest uses of wegen: a full, polite answer in two or three words. Notice that weil cannot do this as easily; a weil-answer needs a subject and a verb. When you are tired or in a hurry, wegen is your friend.

drills.prompt: ___ des Regens bleiben wir drinnen.
drills.hint: You need the word that is followed by a noun, not a clause.
drills.explanation: Wegen des Regens: wegen + genitive. weil needs a whole clause.

drills.prompt: Genitive after wegen: der Lärm → wegen ___ ___
drills.hint: Masculine: des, and the noun gets -s.
drills.explanation: wegen des Lärms

drills.prompt: Wegen ___ Hitze öffnet das Café erst um fünf.
drills.hint: die Hitze is feminine.
drills.explanation: Feminine nouns take der in the genitive: wegen der Hitze.

drills.prompt: Rewrite with wegen: Wir bleiben drinnen, weil es kalt ist. → Wir bleiben wegen ___ ___ drinnen.
drills.hint: kalt → die Kälte, feminine.
drills.explanation: Wir bleiben wegen der Kälte drinnen.

drills.prompt: Wegen des Sturms ___
drills.hint: The wegen-phrase is position 1. What comes next?
drills.explanation: Wegen des Sturms ist das Fest ausgefallen: verb right after position 1.

drills.prompt: Genitive with ein: ein Fehler → wegen ___ ___
drills.hint: ein becomes eines, and the noun gets -s.
drills.explanation: wegen eines Fehlers

blind.prompt: Write in German: Because of the rain only a few people are coming. (start with wegen)
answers: Wegen des Regens kommen nur wenige Leute.
Wegen des Regens kommen nur wenig Leute.
blind.hint: wegen + des …s, then the verb, then the subject.
blind.explanation: Wegen des Regens kommen nur wenige Leute.

check.prompt: Which sentence is the written standard?
options: Wegen des Wetters bleibt das Museum zu.
Wegen dem Wetter bleibt das Museum zu.
Wegen das Wetter bleibt das Museum zu.
check.hint: In writing, wegen takes the genitive.
check.explanation: Wegen des Wetters: genitive. Wegen dem Wetter is spoken German.

check.prompt: Rewrite with wegen: Ben kauft nichts, weil der Preis hoch ist. → Ben kauft wegen ___ ___ nichts.
check.hint: der Preis: masculine, ends in -s, so it gets -es.
check.explanation: Ben kauft wegen des Preises nichts.

check.prompt: Wegen ___ Kosten repariert Ben Robbi selbst.
check.hint: die Kosten is a plural word.
check.explanation: Plural nouns take der in the genitive: wegen der Kosten.

check.prompt: Which sentence has the correct word order?
options: Wegen des Streiks wir fahren mit dem Rad.
Wegen des Streiks fahren wir mit dem Rad.
Wegen des Streiks mit dem Rad fahren wir.
check.hint: After position 1: the verb.
check.explanation: Wegen des Streiks fahren wir mit dem Rad.

check.prompt: Rewrite with wegen: Leon kann nicht lernen, weil es laut ist. → Leon kann wegen ___ ___ nicht lernen.
check.hint: laut → der Lärm, masculine.
check.explanation: Leon kann wegen des Lärms nicht lernen.

check.prompt: Warum ist es heute so leer? – ___
check.hint: A short answer with a noun.
check.explanation: Wegen des Wetters: wegen + genitive works as a short answer.

check.prompt: Wegen ___ Stromausfalls funktioniert der Wasserkocher nicht.
check.hint: der Stromausfall is masculine, and the noun already has -s.
check.explanation: wegen des Stromausfalls

check.prompt: What does 'Meinetwegen!' mean in: Kann ich das Fenster aufmachen? – Meinetwegen!
check.hint: It is a reply to a request.
check.explanation: Meinetwegen = fine by me, I don't mind.

check.prompt: Write the plural article: die Kosten → wegen ___ Kosten
check.hint: Plural nouns in the genitive.
check.explanation: wegen der Kosten

check.prompt: Which reason fits better as a wegen-phrase?
check.hint: wegen likes a clear thing to blame.
check.explanation: Wegen des Stromausfalls … sounds natural; feelings like tiredness usually stay with weil.

examples.de: Wegen des Regens bleiben wir drinnen.
examples.en: Because of the rain we stay inside.

examples.de: Ich komme wegen der Arbeit später.
examples.en: I'm coming later because of work.

examples.de: Die Kosten für die Reparatur sind niedrig.
examples.en: The costs of the repair are low.

examples.de: Wegen der Kosten kauft Ben kein neues Handy.
examples.en: Because of the costs Ben isn't buying a new phone.

examples.de: Der Toaster hat einen Fehler.
examples.en: The toaster has a fault.

examples.de: Im Text sind drei Fehler.
examples.en: There are three mistakes in the text.

examples.de: Gestern hatten wir einen Stromausfall.
examples.en: Yesterday we had a power cut.

examples.de: Wegen des Stromausfalls ist es dunkel.
examples.en: Because of the power cut it is dark.

examples.de: Heute ist ein Streik bei der Bahn.
examples.en: There is a rail strike today.

examples.de: Wegen des Streiks fahren keine Busse.
examples.en: Because of the strike no buses are running.

examples.de: Die Hitze im Sommer ist anstrengend.
examples.en: The heat in summer is tiring.

examples.de: Wegen der Hitze trinken wir viel Wasser.
examples.en: Because of the heat we drink a lot of water.

examples.de: Ich mag die Kälte im Winter nicht.
examples.en: I don't like the cold in winter.

examples.de: Wegen der Kälte trägt Leon Handschuhe.
examples.en: Because of the cold Leon is wearing gloves.

examples.de: In der Nacht gab es einen Sturm.
examples.en: There was a storm in the night.

examples.de: Wegen des Sturms ist das Fest ausgefallen.
examples.en: Because of the storm the party was cancelled.

examples.de: An einem Regentag lese ich gern.
examples.en: On a rainy day I like reading.

examples.de: Heute ist ein typischer Regentag.
examples.en: Today is a typical rainy day.

examples.de: Die Wettervorhersage sagt Regen.
examples.en: The forecast says rain.

examples.de: Hast du die Wettervorhersage gesehen?
examples.en: Have you seen the weather forecast?

examples.de: Draußen ist es nass und ungemütlich.
examples.en: Outside it is wet and unpleasant.

examples.de: Der Raum ist kalt und ungemütlich.
examples.en: The room is cold and uncomfortable.

examples.de: Meine Jacke ist ganz nass.
examples.en: My jacket is completely wet.

examples.de: Wegen des Regens ist die Straße nass.
examples.en: Because of the rain the street is wet.

examples.de: Leon trägt warme Handschuhe.
examples.en: Leon is wearing warm gloves.

examples.de: Wo sind meine Handschuhe?
examples.en: Where are my gloves?

examples.de: Kann ich das Licht ausmachen? – Meinetwegen.
examples.en: Can I turn off the light? – Fine by me.

examples.de: Meinetwegen können wir später essen.
examples.en: As far as I'm concerned we can eat later.

prompts: Say why something was cancelled or late this week. Use wegen twice: once in position 1, once in the middle.
Turn three weil-sentences about the weather into wegen-sentences.
Answer the question 'Warum bist du heute zu Hause?' with a short wegen-answer, then a full sentence.
examples: Wegen des Streiks bin ich am Montag mit dem Rad gefahren. Mein Deutschkurs ist wegen eines Fehlers im System ausgefallen.

Weil es regnet, bleibe ich drinnen. → Wegen des Regens bleibe ich drinnen. Weil es heiß ist, schlafe ich schlecht. → Wegen der Hitze schlafe ich schlecht. Weil es kalt ist, trage ich Handschuhe. → Wegen der Kälte trage ich Handschuhe.
Wegen des Wetters. Es ist nass und ungemütlich, deshalb bleibe ich heute zu Hause.

retrieval.explanation: Ben lässt Robbi im Repair-Café reparieren.

retrieval.hint: A result word, verb right after it.
