Review: Robbi war so laut, ___ niemand schlafen konnte.
retrieval.hint: so … ___: the result, verb at the end.
retrieval.explanation: so laut, dass niemand schlafen konnte.

lessons.title: Trotz des Regens – trotzdem: contrast
lessons.goal: Say that something happens against expectations in three ways: obwohl + clause, trotzdem + verb, trotz + genitive, and keep trotz and trotzdem apart.

grammar.point: trotz means 'despite' and takes the genitive like wegen: trotz des Regens, trotz der Kälte. The same contrast has three shapes: obwohl + clause (verb at the end), trotzdem + verb (new main sentence), trotz + noun. trotz always needs a noun; trotzdem stands alone, because -dem already points back to the reason.
grammar.oneLine: Trotz des Regens gehen wir spazieren.

mistake.wrong: Trotzdem des Regens gehen wir spazieren.
mistake.right: Trotz des Regens gehen wir spazieren.
mistake.why: trotzdem already means "despite that" and stands alone. Before a noun use the preposition trotz.

terms.meaning: 'despite' + des/der: the contrast as a noun
something happens against what you expect
written word for trotzdem

cards.title: Before we start: from 'wegen' to its opposite 'trotz'
cards.body: Rain usually keeps people at home. But sometimes they come anyway. That is a contrast: something happens against what you expect. You already have two tools for it, obwohl and trotzdem. Today you get a third one, the twin of wegen: trotz + genitive. Then you can say the same contrast in three ways.
steps: You already know: Wegen des Regens bleiben wir drinnen (lesson 10), Es regnet. Trotzdem gehen wir. (A2) and Obwohl es regnet, … (B1 chapter 1).
New today: trotz + genitive: Trotz des Regens gehen wir.
By the end you can: say one contrast with obwohl, trotzdem and trotz, and never mix up trotz and trotzdem.

examples.de: Es regnet. Trotzdem gehen wir.
examples.en: It's raining. We're going anyway.
examples.why: You know this already: trotzdem, verb next.

examples.de: Trotz des Regens gehen wir.
examples.en: Despite the rain we're going.
examples.why: New today: trotz + a noun in the genitive.

cards.more: Think of a river and a swimmer. Wegen is the swimmer going with the current: it rains, so people stay at home, exactly as expected. Trotz is the swimmer going against the current: it rains, and people still come. German loves this second picture and gives you three ways to paint it. One you know from A2, one from last chapter, and one is new today. They all say the same thing; they only build the sentence differently. Let's line them up.

cards.title: trotz + genitive: despite something
cards.body: trotz means 'despite, in spite of'. Like wegen it takes the genitive: trotz des Regens, trotz des Preises, trotz der Kälte, trotz der Probleme. The pattern is the same as yesterday: des …s for masculine and neuter, der for feminine and plural.
cards.lead: Yesterday wegen gave a reason with a genitive noun. This card brings its opposite, trotz, which uses exactly the same genitive forms.

examples.de: Trotz des Regens ist die Stimmung gut.
examples.en: Despite the rain the atmosphere is good.

examples.de: Trotz der Kälte sitzt Anna draußen.
examples.en: Despite the cold Anna is sitting outside.

examples.de: Ben kauft den Saugroboter trotz des Preises.
examples.en: Ben buys the robot vacuum despite the price.

deeper.text: Two useful extras. First, trotz allem means 'despite everything', a very common fixed phrase: Trotz allem war es ein schöner Tag. Second, as with wegen, people in everyday speech, especially in Austria and southern Germany, often use the dative: trotz dem Regen. In writing and in this course use the genitive, the written standard.

example.de: Trotz allem war es ein schöner Tag.
example.en: Despite everything it was a nice day.

cards.more: Good news: there is nothing new to learn about the endings. Take everything you did with wegen yesterday and swap one word. Wegen des Regens bleiben wir drinnen becomes Trotz des Regens gehen wir raus. Same genitive, opposite meaning. In English, 'despite' and 'in spite of' also take a noun, so this one feels quite natural. Say a few pairs aloud: wegen der Kälte, trotz der Kälte; wegen des Preises, trotz des Preises. Your mouth learns the pattern twice in one go.

cards.title: wegen or trotz? Expected or unexpected
cards.body: Ask one question: does the result follow the reason, or go against it? Expected → wegen: Wegen des Regens bleiben wir zu Hause. Unexpected → trotz: Trotz des Regens gehen wir spazieren. The noun is the same; only the direction of the arrow changes.
cards.lead: You know both little words now. This card helps you choose between them: wegen when things go as expected, trotz when they don't.

examples.de: Wegen der Hitze bleibt Mira zu Hause.
examples.en: Because of the heat Mira stays at home.

examples.de: Trotz der Hitze joggt Leon im Park.
examples.en: Despite the heat Leon goes jogging in the park.

examples.de: Trotz des Lärms kann Ben gut schlafen.
examples.en: Despite the noise Ben can sleep well.

steps: Name the reason: der Regen.
Ask: does the result follow it (expected) or go against it (unexpected)?
Expected → wegen; unexpected → trotz.

deeper.text: The noun Trotz also exists on its own and means 'defiance', the stubborn feeling of doing something because someone said no. Parents in Germany talk about the Trotzphase, the 'terrible twos', when small children say Nein! to everything. So trotz always carries a little of that stubborn spirit: something happens anyway, against all reasons.

example.de: Unser Sohn ist in der Trotzphase.
example.en: Our son is in the terrible twos.

cards.more: Draw two arrows in your notebook. Arrow one: rain → stay home. Straight, logical, no surprise: wegen. Arrow two: rain → go for a walk. It bends against the logic: trotz. Whenever you are unsure, say the sentence in English with 'because of' and then with 'despite'. Only one of them makes sense. Because of the heat Leon goes jogging? Strange. Despite the heat Leon goes jogging? Yes. Your English sense of surprise is a reliable guide here.

cards.title: One contrast, three ways
cards.body: The same contrast in three sentences. obwohl starts a side clause: the verb goes to the END. trotzdem starts a new main sentence: the verb comes NEXT. trotz takes only a NOUN in the genitive, then the verb follows. All three mean: it rains, but many people come.
cards.lead: You can choose between wegen and trotz. Now line up all your contrast tools side by side: obwohl, trotzdem and the new trotz.

examples.de: Obwohl es regnet, kommen viele Leute.
examples.en: Although it's raining, many people come.

examples.de: Es regnet. Trotzdem kommen viele Leute.
examples.en: It's raining. Many people come anyway.

examples.de: Trotz des Regens kommen viele Leute.
examples.en: Despite the rain many people come.

rows: Obwohl es regnet, kommen viele Leute.
Es regnet. Trotzdem kommen viele Leute.
Trotz des Regens kommen viele Leute.

deeper.text: All three can also move. The obwohl-clause can come second: Viele Leute kommen, obwohl es regnet. trotzdem can stand after the verb, often with aber: Es regnet, aber viele Leute kommen trotzdem. And the trotz-phrase can sit in the middle: Viele Leute kommen trotz des Regens. Positions change; the rules for the verb stay the same.

example.de: Es regnet, aber viele Leute kommen trotzdem.
example.en: It's raining, but many people come anyway.

cards.more: Think of three different doors into the same room. Door one, obwohl, is a long corridor: you walk through a whole side clause and the verb waits at the far end. Door two, trotzdem, is a hinge between two sentences: first a full stop, then trotzdem, then the verb. Door three, trotz, is the shortcut: just one noun, no extra verb. The room behind the doors is always the same. Choose the door that fits your sentence: a clause, two sentences, or one noun.

cards.title: trotz or trotzdem? Never both together
cards.body: trotz is a preposition: it always needs a noun after it (trotz des Regens). trotzdem is an adverb: it stands alone and the noun is gone, because dem already points back to the reason (trotzdem = despite that). So never write trotzdem des Regens.
cards.lead: You have seen trotz and trotzdem in the table. This card fixes the one mix-up that almost every learner makes between these two look-alikes.

examples.de: Trotz des Preises kauft Mira das Handy.
examples.en: Despite the price Mira buys the phone.

examples.de: Das Handy ist teuer. Trotzdem kauft Mira es.
examples.en: The phone is expensive. Mira buys it anyway.

examples.de: Trotz der Kosten ist Frau Weber zufrieden.
examples.en: Despite the costs Frau Weber is satisfied.

deeper.text: trotzdem also works as a one-word answer, and it often sounds a bit stubborn: Es regnet! – Trotzdem! (I'm going anyway!). In written, formal German you will also meet dennoch, which means the same as trotzdem and follows the same word order: Der Preis ist hoch. Dennoch kaufen viele Leute das Gerät. Use trotzdem when you speak; recognise dennoch in texts.

example.de: Der Preis ist hoch. Dennoch kaufen viele Leute das Gerät.
example.en: The price is high. Nevertheless many people buy the device.

cards.more: Look inside the word: trotz-dem. The -dem part is like the English 'that' in 'despite that'. It already holds the reason you said before. So trotzdem is a full package: preposition plus 'that'. If you add des Regens after it, you say the reason twice: 'despite that of the rain'. Simple test: is there a noun right after the word? Then you need plain trotz. Is the reason already in the sentence before? Then trotzdem, alone.

cards.title: The chapter's logic map
cards.body: Six words, two jobs, three shapes. Reason (expected): weil + clause, deshalb + verb, wegen + noun. Contrast (unexpected): obwohl + clause, trotzdem + verb, trotz + noun. Each column has the same word order. Learn them as pairs: weil ↔ obwohl, deshalb ↔ trotzdem, wegen ↔ trotz.
cards.lead: Now you know trotz and trotzdem apart. This card puts all six connectors of this chapter on one map, so you can see the pairs.

examples.de: Weil der Akku leer ist, fährt Robbi nicht.
examples.en: Because the battery is empty, Robbi doesn't drive.

examples.de: Obwohl der Akku leer ist, fährt Robbi weiter.
examples.en: Although the battery is empty, Robbi keeps driving.

examples.de: Wegen des Regens bleibt Leon zu Hause.
examples.en: Because of the rain Leon stays at home.

deeper.text: A real-life tip: in a written comment, mix the three shapes. A text with only weil and obwohl sounds like a list. Write one weil-clause, one deshalb-sentence and one wegen-phrase, and your German suddenly sounds like B1. Examiners in the Goethe exam reward exactly this variety, which they call 'Kohärenz' (how well the text holds together).

example.de: Wegen der Kosten repariere ich alles selbst.
example.en: Because of the costs I repair everything myself.

cards.more: Think of a chessboard with two rows and three columns. The top row is 'as expected', the bottom row is 'surprise'. Each column is a piece that moves in its own way: the clause piece pushes the verb to the end, the adverb piece pulls the verb next to it, the noun piece only wants a genitive. Once you know how one piece in a column moves, you know its partner too. That is why learning them in pairs saves you half the work.

cards.title: Ben: Trotz der Probleme mag ich Robbi
cards.body: Read Ben's short text about Robbi. Find two trotz-phrases, one trotzdem and one wegen. Which surprise does each contrast show?
cards.lead: You have the whole logic map now. Read it in action in Ben's honest little text about his robot vacuum and all its trouble.

examples.de: Trotz der Probleme mag ich Robbi.
examples.en: Despite the problems I like Robbi.

examples.de: Er ist laut. Trotzdem schläft meine Katze neben ihm.
examples.en: He is loud. My cat sleeps next to him anyway.

examples.de: Trotz des Preises hat sich der Kauf gelohnt.
examples.en: Despite the price the purchase was worth it.

steps: Trotz der Probleme mag ich Robbi.
Er ist laut. Trotzdem schläft meine Katze neben ihm.
Wegen des Akkus fährt er nur zwanzig Minuten.
Trotz des Preises hat sich der Kauf gelohnt.
Und seit dem Repair-Café ist er sogar fast leise!

deeper.text: Look at the verb sich lohnen, 'to be worth it'. Germans use it constantly when they talk about money and effort: Das lohnt sich (it's worth it), Das lohnt sich nicht (it's not worth it). With repairs it is the key question: Lohnt sich die Reparatur? The answer often comes with trotz: Trotz der Kosten lohnt sich die Reparatur.

example.de: Lohnt sich die Reparatur?
example.en: Is the repair worth it?

cards.more: Imagine Ben telling this at the WG kitchen table, half laughing. Every sentence has a little twist: the robot is loud, but the cat loves it; it cost a lot, but it was worth it. That twist is exactly what trotz and trotzdem are for. Read the text twice: first for the story, then with a pencil, marking every contrast word. Then try to retell it to yourself in your own words, using at least one trotz and one trotzdem.

drills.prompt: ___ des Regens gehen wir spazieren.
drills.hint: A noun follows: you need the preposition.
drills.explanation: Trotz des Regens: trotz + genitive.

drills.prompt: Genitive after trotz: die Kälte → trotz ___ ___
drills.hint: Feminine noun.
drills.explanation: trotz der Kälte

drills.prompt: Es ist kalt. ___ sitzt Anna draußen.
drills.hint: A new sentence, no noun after the gap, verb next.
drills.explanation: Trotzdem sitzt Anna draußen.

drills.prompt: Wegen or trotz? ___ des Lärms kann Ben gut schlafen.
drills.hint: Sleeping well with noise: expected or a surprise?
drills.explanation: Trotz des Lärms: the result goes against the reason.

drills.prompt: Turn the clause into a noun phrase: Obwohl der Preis hoch ist, kauft Mira das Handy. → ___ ___ ___ kauft Mira das Handy.
drills.hint: The preposition for 'despite' + der Preis in the genitive.
drills.explanation: Trotz des Preises kauft Mira das Handy.

drills.prompt: Obwohl es regnet, ___
drills.hint: After the obwohl-clause: the main verb comes first.
drills.explanation: Obwohl es regnet, kommen viele Leute.

blind.prompt: Write in German: Despite the rain the atmosphere is good. (start with trotz)
answers: Trotz des Regens ist die Stimmung gut.
Trotz des Regens ist die Atmosphäre gut.
blind.hint: trotz + des …s, then the verb, then the subject.
blind.explanation: Trotz des Regens ist die Stimmung gut.

check.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Trotz des Regens gehen wir spazieren.
Trotzdem des Regens gehen wir spazieren.
Trotz der Regen gehen wir spazieren.
check.hint: Before a noun: the preposition, then genitive.
check.explanation: Trotz des Regens: trotz + genitive. trotzdem never takes a noun.

check.prompt: Trotz ___ Probleme mag Ben Robbi.
check.hint: die Probleme is plural.
check.explanation: Plural genitive: trotz der Probleme.

check.prompt: Rewrite as two sentences: Obwohl es laut ist, schläft die Katze. → Es ist laut. ___ schläft die Katze. (anyway)
check.hint: The adverb: new sentence, verb next.
check.explanation: Es ist laut. Trotzdem schläft die Katze.

check.prompt: Which word means 'because of', not 'despite'?
check.hint: Expected result.
check.explanation: wegen = because of. trotz and obwohl show a contrast.

check.prompt: Der Akku ist schwach. Trotzdem ___
check.hint: trotzdem is position 1: what comes next?
check.explanation: Trotzdem fährt Robbi weiter.

check.prompt: Rewrite with trotz: Obwohl es kalt ist, joggt Leon. → Trotz ___ ___ joggt Leon.
check.hint: kalt → die Kälte.
check.explanation: Trotz der Kälte joggt Leon.

check.prompt: Which pair belongs together on the logic map?
check.hint: Both pull the verb straight after them.
check.explanation: deshalb (reason) ↔ trotzdem (contrast): both adverbs, verb next.

check.prompt: ___ das Wetter schlecht ist, ist die Stimmung gut.
check.hint: A whole clause follows, verb at the end.
check.explanation: Obwohl das Wetter schlecht ist, …: obwohl + clause.

check.prompt: Genitive after trotz: der Preis → trotz ___ ___
check.hint: Masculine, ends in -s, so -es.
check.explanation: trotz des Preises

check.prompt: What does dennoch mean in: Der Preis ist hoch. Dennoch kaufen viele Leute das Gerät.
check.hint: It is the written twin of trotzdem.
check.explanation: dennoch = trotzdem, nevertheless.

examples.de: Trotz des Regens gehen wir spazieren.
examples.en: Despite the rain we go for a walk.

examples.de: Trotz der Kälte sitzt Anna draußen.
examples.en: Despite the cold Anna sits outside.

examples.de: Trotz allem war es ein schöner Abend.
examples.en: Despite everything it was a nice evening.

examples.de: Trotz allem bin ich zufrieden.
examples.en: Despite everything I'm satisfied.

examples.de: Es war teuer. Dennoch hat es sich gelohnt.
examples.en: It was expensive. Nevertheless it was worth it.

examples.de: Der Weg ist lang. Dennoch kommen viele.
examples.en: The way is long. Nevertheless many come.

examples.de: Ben hat Schwierigkeiten mit der Anleitung.
examples.en: Ben has difficulties with the instructions.

examples.de: Das ist keine große Schwierigkeit.
examples.en: That is no big difficulty.

examples.de: Die Reparatur ist viel Aufwand.
examples.en: The repair is a lot of effort.

examples.de: Der Aufwand ist zu groß.
examples.en: The effort is too great.

examples.de: Die Reparatur lohnt sich.
examples.en: The repair is worth it.

examples.de: Lohnt sich das neue Handy?
examples.en: Is the new phone worth it?

examples.de: Leon gibt sich viel Mühe.
examples.en: Leon makes a lot of effort.

examples.de: Das ist nicht der Mühe wert.
examples.en: That's not worth the trouble.

examples.de: Das Ergebnis ist überraschend.
examples.en: The result is surprising.

examples.de: Überraschend viele Leute sind gekommen.
examples.en: Surprisingly many people came.

examples.de: Der Besuch war unerwartet.
examples.en: The visit was unexpected.

examples.de: Das Problem kam ganz unerwartet.
examples.en: The problem came quite unexpectedly.

examples.de: Meine Erwartungen waren hoch.
examples.en: My expectations were high.

examples.de: Robbi hat die Erwartungen nicht erfüllt.
examples.en: Robbi didn't meet the expectations.

examples.de: Die Kinder malen mit Begeisterung.
examples.en: The children paint with enthusiasm.

examples.de: Trotz des Regens ist die Begeisterung groß.
examples.en: Despite the rain the enthusiasm is great.

examples.de: Die Reparatur ist gelungen.
examples.en: The repair worked out.

examples.de: Der Kuchen ist mir gut gelungen.
examples.en: My cake turned out well.

examples.de: Robbi fährt um das Hindernis herum.
examples.en: Robbi drives around the obstacle.

examples.de: Trotz aller Hindernisse hat sie es geschafft.
examples.en: Despite all obstacles she made it.

examples.de: Unser Sohn ist in der Trotzphase.
examples.en: Our son is in the defiant phase.

examples.de: Die Trotzphase ist anstrengend.
examples.en: The defiant phase is exhausting.

prompts: Tell about a day when you did something despite bad weather. Use trotz once and trotzdem once.
Say one contrast from your life in three ways: with obwohl, trotzdem and trotz.
Name something that was expensive but worth it. Use sich lohnen.
examples: Letzten Sonntag hat es stark geregnet. Trotz des Regens bin ich in den Park gegangen. Ich war ganz nass. Trotzdem war es schön.
Obwohl es kalt ist, fahre ich mit dem Rad. Es ist kalt. Trotzdem fahre ich mit dem Rad. Trotz der Kälte fahre ich mit dem Rad.
Mein Laptop war teuer. Trotz des Preises hat sich der Kauf gelohnt, weil ich jeden Tag damit arbeite.

retrieval.prompt: Review: written standard after wegen: der Regen → wegen ___ ___
Review: In speech many people say wegen ___ Regen.
retrieval.hint: The spoken form uses the dative.
retrieval.explanation: wegen dem Regen (spoken); written: wegen des Regens.

retrieval.prompt: Review: Leon ___ sein Fahrrad im Laden reparieren. (have done)
Review: Der Akku ist leer. ___ funktioniert Robbi nicht.
retrieval.hint: A result word that starts with des-.

lessons.title: Reparieren oder neu kaufen?: reasons, counter-reasons and a comment
lessons.goal: Give reasons and counter-reasons with all the chapter connectors, write a forum comment in four steps, and pronounce ts and tst.

grammar.point: No new grammar: combine weil/da (verb at the end), deshalb/trotzdem (verb next), wegen/trotz + genitive and obwohl in one text. A comment has four steps: opinion (Ich finde, dass …), reason + example, counter-reason (Das stimmt, aber … / Andererseits …), conclusion (Deshalb … / Alles in allem …). After dass a modal goes to the very end: dass man reparieren sollte.
grammar.oneLine: Ich finde, dass man mehr reparieren sollte.

mistake.wrong: Ich finde, dass man sollte reparieren.
mistake.right: Ich finde, dass man reparieren sollte.
mistake.why: dass sends the finite verb to the end. With a modal, the infinitive comes first and the modal is last.

terms.meaning: reason for / reason against
opinion, reason + example, counter-reason, conclusion
the sounds in trotz, jetzt and du sitzt

cards.title: Before we start: from single reasons to a real discussion
cards.body: Robbi is repaired, and the Kiez forum asks a big question: Reparieren oder neu kaufen? Today there is no new grammar. Instead you put all your connectors together: weil, deshalb, wegen, obwohl, trotzdem, trotz. With them you can write a real forum comment, and you practise two sounds that are everywhere in these words: ts and tst.
steps: You already know: weil/da, deshalb/darum, wegen/trotz, obwohl/trotzdem and einerseits … andererseits (A2).
New today: phrases for reasons and counter-reasons, a four-step comment, and the sounds ts and tst.
By the end you can: write a short forum comment with an opinion, a reason, a counter-reason and a conclusion.

examples.de: Ich repariere Robbi, weil das billiger ist.
examples.en: I repair Robbi because it is cheaper.
examples.why: You know this already: one reason with weil.

examples.de: Ein Grund dafür ist, dass Reparieren billiger ist.
examples.en: One reason for it is that repairing is cheaper.
examples.why: New today: a phrase that introduces a reason in a discussion.

cards.more: Think of a football team. Until now you trained each player alone: weil passes the ball one way, trotzdem another, wegen yet another. Today the whole team plays a match together. A forum comment is that match: you need an opinion, a good reason, a fair counter-reason and a clear end. Nothing new to memorise about word order. The skill today is choosing the right player at the right moment, and speaking the ts and tst sounds clearly while you do it.

cards.title: Reparieren oder neu kaufen? Three comments
cards.body: Read three comments from the Kiez forum. Ben prefers buying new. Frau Weber wants to repair, because of the environment. Mira says: it depends on the price. Mark every connector you find.
cards.lead: You know all the connectors of this chapter. This card shows them in three real opinions from the WG and the neighbourhood forum.

examples.de: Neu kaufen ist einfacher. Deshalb kaufe ich meistens neu.
examples.en: Buying new is easier. That's why I mostly buy new.

examples.de: Wegen der Umwelt repariere ich lieber.
examples.en: Because of the environment I prefer to repair.

examples.de: Das hängt vom Preis ab.
examples.en: That depends on the price.

steps: Ben: Ehrlich gesagt kaufe ich lieber neu. Eine Reparatur dauert lange, und oft gibt es keine Ersatzteile. Deshalb kaufe ich meistens ein neues Gerät.
Frau Weber: Ich repariere fast alles, wegen der Umwelt. Neue Geräte brauchen viele Rohstoffe. Trotz des Aufwands lohnt sich das.
Mira: Das hängt vom Preis ab. Wenn die Reparatur billig ist, repariere ich. Wenn sie teuer ist, kaufe ich neu.

deeper.text: The word Wegwerfgesellschaft (throwaway society) is a typical German compound: wegwerfen (throw away) + die Gesellschaft (society). The last part always decides the gender, so it is die Wegwerfgesellschaft. Germans build such words freely in discussions about the environment. You can take them apart like Lego: first find the last noun, then read the parts before it as its description.

example.de: Wir leben in einer Wegwerfgesellschaft.
example.en: We live in a throwaway society.

cards.more: Imagine three neighbours on a bench. Ben is practical and a little lazy: new is quick. Frau Weber thinks of the future: less rubbish, fewer new devices. Mira is the calculator: she looks at the numbers first. Nobody is wrong; they simply weigh things differently. When you read a forum, ask for each person: what is their opinion, and which word shows their reason? You will find weil, deshalb, wegen and trotzdem doing the work behind every opinion.

cards.title: Pro and contra: phrases for a discussion
cards.body: To discuss, you need phrases that announce a reason or a counter-reason. Pro: Ein Grund dafür ist, dass … / Dafür spricht, dass … Contra: Dagegen spricht, dass … / Das stimmt, aber … And with two sides: Einerseits …, andererseits …
cards.lead: You have read three opinions. This card gives you the phrases those opinions are built with, for reasons and counter-reasons.

examples.de: Dafür spricht, dass Reparieren billiger ist.
examples.en: One argument for it is that repairing is cheaper.

examples.de: Dagegen spricht, dass es lange dauert.
examples.en: Against it is that it takes a long time.

examples.de: Einerseits ist ein neues Handy schnell, andererseits ist es teuer.
examples.en: On the one hand a new phone is fast, on the other hand it is expensive.

deeper.text: In German discussions open disagreement is normal and not rude. People say Da muss ich widersprechen (I have to disagree there) or Das sehe ich anders (I see that differently) quite directly, even to older people. The politeness is in the facts and the tone, not in avoiding a clear no. So don't be afraid to say Das stimmt nicht ganz.

example.de: Das sehe ich anders.
example.en: I see that differently.

cards.more: Think of an old pair of kitchen scales. On the left pan you put the arguments dafür, on the right pan the arguments dagegen. Each phrase on this card is a hand that puts one weight on a pan. Dafür spricht, dass … drops a weight on the left. Dagegen spricht, dass … drops one on the right. Das stimmt, aber … first touches the other pan politely, then adds to yours. A good comment shows both pans before it says which side is heavier.

cards.title: A comment in four steps
cards.body: A good comment has four steps. 1 Opinion: Ich finde, dass … 2 Reason + example: weil …, zum Beispiel … 3 Counter-reason: Das stimmt, aber … / Andererseits … 4 Conclusion: Deshalb finde ich … Remember: after dass the verb goes to the end, also a modal: dass man reparieren sollte.
cards.lead: You have the phrases now. This card shows how to order them, so that your comment is clear and easy to follow from start to end.

examples.de: Ich finde, dass man alte Geräte reparieren sollte.
examples.en: I think that people should repair old devices.

examples.de: Andererseits sind manche Reparaturen sehr teuer.
examples.en: On the other hand some repairs are very expensive.

examples.de: Deshalb finde ich einen Kompromiss am besten.
examples.en: That's why I think a compromise is best.

steps: Opinion: Ich finde, dass …
Reason + example: …, weil … Zum Beispiel …
Counter-reason: Das stimmt, aber … / Andererseits …
Conclusion: Deshalb finde ich … / Alles in allem …

deeper.text: For the roof, two more useful openers: Alles in allem … (all in all) and Zum Schluss möchte ich sagen, dass … (finally I'd like to say that …). Both are typical in Goethe B1 writing. Alles in allem behaves like deshalb: the verb comes right after it. Use one of them to show the reader clearly that your conclusion starts now.

example.de: Alles in allem lohnt sich die Reparatur.
example.en: All in all the repair is worth it.

cards.more: Think of building a small house. Step 1 is the foundation: your opinion. Step 2 builds the walls: a reason and a concrete example, like your own broken toaster. Step 3 is the window: you look out and see the other side. Step 4 is the roof that holds it all together: Deshalb finde ich … Without a roof the house feels unfinished; without a window it feels closed and stubborn. Readers trust a writer who shows the other side before deciding.

cards.title: The sound [ts]: z, tz, ts, ds, tion
cards.body: Five spellings, one sound: [ts], like the end of English 'cats'. z: Zeit, zu. tz: jetzt, trotz. ts: nichts, rechts. ds: abends. -tion: Information, Funktion. So trotz and trotzdem both start and end with a sharp ts-sound.
cards.lead: You can write a comment now. To say it aloud, this card trains the sound that hides in trotz, jetzt and nichts: the sharp [ts].

examples.de: Jetzt habe ich keine Zeit.
examples.en: I have no time now.

examples.de: Trotz des Regens kommen jetzt zehn Leute.
examples.en: Despite the rain ten people are coming now.

examples.de: Abends ist die Reparatur fertig.
examples.en: In the evening the repair is ready.

deeper.text: Words ending in -tion are always feminine and the stress is on the last syllable, on -on: die Information, die Funktion. So the -tion ending gives you two free rules at once: the sound [tsjo:n] and the article die. That helps in forums, where many such words appear: die Diskussion, die Situation.

example.de: Die Funktion ist einfach.
example.en: The function is simple.

cards.more: Put your tongue behind your top teeth and say 't', then let the air hiss out as 's', fast, in one go: ts. That is the whole sound. English has it only at the end of words like 'cats' or 'it's', so English speakers often say a soft 's' or 'z' at the start of German words. Zeit is not 'site' or 'zite': it is tsait. Try a little chain: Zeit, jetzt, nichts, abends, Funktion. Same hiss five times.

cards.title: The sound [tst]: du sitzt, du lässt, jetzt
cards.body: Add a t after ts and you get [tst]. You hear it in du-forms of verbs ending in -tz, -ss or -ß (du sitzt, du nutzt, du ersetzt, du lässt), and in jetzt, zuletzt, der letzte. Tongue twister: Jetzt putzt du zuletzt und lässt nichts liegen.
cards.lead: You can say the sharp [ts] now. Add one more t and you get [tst], the sound of many du-forms and of words like jetzt.

examples.de: Du lässt dein Handy reparieren?
examples.en: You're having your phone repaired?

examples.de: Du nutzt jetzt das alte Handy.
examples.en: You're using the old phone now.

examples.de: Du ersetzt den Akku selbst.
examples.en: You replace the battery yourself.

steps: Slowly: du sit – s – t
Faster: du sitzt, du nutzt, du ersetzt
With an umlaut: du lässt
Chant: Jetzt putzt du zuletzt und lässt nichts liegen.

deeper.text: Why is it du lässt and not du lässst? German does not write the s of the du-ending -st twice when the verb already ends in an s-sound. lassen → du lässt, sitzen → du sitzt, heißen → du heißt. So the spelling hides one s, but the mouth still says the same [st] ending. The same happens with ersetzen and nutzen.

example.de: Wie heißt du?
example.en: What's your name?

cards.more: Think of a tiny drum roll: t-s-t. Your tongue taps the teeth, the air hisses, and the tongue taps again. Many learners drop the middle s and say 'du sit' or drop the last t. Slow it down first: du sit-s-t. Then faster: du sitzt. Then the chant: Jetzt putzt du zuletzt und lässt nichts liegen. Say it three times, getting a little faster each time. If you can say it without stopping, every du-form in this chapter will be easy.

cards.title: Frau Weber's model comment
cards.body: Read Frau Weber's comment in the forum. Find the four steps: opinion, reason with example, counter-reason, conclusion. Which connectors does she use for each step?
cards.lead: You have the four steps and the sounds. Now see a full comment in about ninety words, written by Frau Weber for the Kiez forum.

examples.de: Ich finde, dass man mehr reparieren sollte.
examples.en: I think people should repair more.

examples.de: Trotz der Kosten lohnt sich das.
examples.en: Despite the costs it's worth it.

examples.de: Alles in allem repariere ich lieber.
examples.en: All in all I prefer to repair.

steps: Hallo zusammen! Ich finde, dass man mehr reparieren sollte.
Wegen der Umwelt ist das wichtig: Ein neues Gerät braucht viele Rohstoffe, und das alte wird Elektroschrott.
Zum Beispiel hat unser Repair-Café letzte Woche zwölf Toaster repariert.
Das stimmt, manchmal ist eine Reparatur teuer, und sie dauert lange. Trotz der Kosten lohnt sich das oft, weil das Gerät dann noch viele Jahre funktioniert.
Alles in allem repariere ich lieber. Was meint ihr?

deeper.text: In German online forums people usually write du or ihr to each other, even when they don't know each other, and start with Hallo zusammen or Hallo ihr Lieben. In emails to a landlord or a shop you use Sie. So the forum is informal, but the arguments can still be serious. Frau Weber, who is older, writes informally here too.

example.de: Hallo zusammen! Was meint ihr?
example.en: Hello everyone! What do you think?

cards.more: Imagine you are the teacher, holding a red and a green pen. Read Frau Weber's comment once for the content. Then underline each step in a different colour: opinion, reason, counter-reason, conclusion. Circle every connector: dass, wegen, zum Beispiel, obwohl, trotzdem, alles in allem. You will see that almost every sentence has one. That is not an accident; it is what makes the comment easy to read. Your own comment on the skill day can follow exactly this plan.

lessons.title: Nie wieder putzen!: comparing ads and giving an opinion
lessons.goal: Describe and compare two ads, the TechnoMax ad for Robbi and Anna's Repair-Café poster, and say clearly what you think of them with Meiner Meinung nach, Ich finde, dass … and deshalb.

grammar.topic: Comparing ads and giving an opinion: comparatives, Meiner Meinung nach + verb, deshalb in ad sentences
grammar.point: To compare two ads, use the comparative + als: Die Anzeige ist bunter als das Plakat. For the best one: Am besten gefällt mir … After Meiner Meinung nach the verb comes next, because the phrase fills position 1. After Ich finde, dass … the verb goes to the end. deshalb gives the result of a promise.
grammar.oneLine: Meiner Meinung nach ist das Plakat ehrlicher als die Anzeige.

mistake.wrong: Meiner Meinung nach die Werbung ist ehrlich.
mistake.right: Meiner Meinung nach ist die Werbung ehrlich.
mistake.why: Meiner Meinung nach fills position 1 on its own, so the verb ist must come next, before the subject.

terms.meaning: the 'more' form of an adjective: bunt → bunter, ehrlich → ehrlicher; with als for the second thing
the first slot of a main clause; Meiner Meinung nach fills it, so the verb comes straight after
a short, easy sentence that an ad repeats: Nie wieder putzen!

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Robbi ist laut' to 'Robbi in der Werbung'
cards.body: Robbi has had a busy chapter: Ben ordered him, he broke, and the Repair-Café fixed him. Today we look at him from the outside, in an ad. You compare the TechnoMax ad with Anna's poster for the Repair-Café and say clearly what you think. You see ads every day, so these words are useful at once.
steps: You already know: Robbi ist lauter als der Kühlschrank. Meiner Meinung nach ist das gut.
New today: words for ads (die Anzeige, das Plakat, der Slogan …) and phrases to judge an ad.
By the end you can: describe two ads, compare them and give your opinion with a reason.

examples.de: Robbi ist lauter als der Kühlschrank.
examples.en: Robbi is louder than the fridge.
examples.why: You know this: a comparative with als.

examples.de: Die Anzeige ist bunter als das Plakat.
examples.en: The ad is more colourful than the poster.
examples.why: New today: the same comparative, now about ads.

cards.more: Think about your way to work this morning. You probably passed a poster at the bus stop, a flyer in the letterbox and a short video before a song online. All of these try to make you buy or do something. Today you learn the names of these ads and how to talk about them like a critic: which one is louder, which one is more honest, and which one you like best. The grammar is old friends, the comparative and Meiner Meinung nach.

cards.title: Words for ads
cards.lead: We start with names. Before you can compare two ads, you need words for the different kinds of ads and for the parts that every ad has, like the slogan and the target group.
cards.body: die Werbung is advertising in general. One ad in a newspaper or online is die Anzeige. A big paper ad on a wall is das Plakat, a small paper one is der Flyer. On TV or YouTube it is der Werbespot. Every ad has a Produkt, a Slogan and a Zielgruppe: the people it wants to reach.

examples.de: TechnoMax hat eine Anzeige für Robbi im Internet.
examples.en: TechnoMax has an ad for Robbi on the internet.

examples.de: Anna hängt das Plakat im Gemeindehaus auf.
examples.en: Anna puts up the poster in the community hall.

examples.de: Die Zielgruppe des Werbespots sind junge Leute.
examples.en: The commercial's target group is young people.

deeper.text: Careful with die Anzeige: it has two meanings. In an ad context it is an advertisement, but eine Anzeige bei der Polizei is a report to the police, as in the travel chapter. The context always tells you which one. Also: Germans say der Flyer and der Slogan, English loan words, but they write the plural the German way: die Flyer without -s, die Slogans with -s.

example.de: Ich habe die Anzeige in der Zeitung gesehen.
example.en: I saw the ad in the newspaper.

cards.more: Sort the words by size and place. Small and in your hand: der Flyer, you take it from a café table. Big and on the street: das Plakat, you see it at the U-Bahn. In a newspaper or on a website: die Anzeige. Moving pictures with sound: der Werbespot. Then three words that every ad needs, whatever its size: das Produkt is the thing it sells, der Slogan is the short sentence you remember, and die Zielgruppe is the people the ad is talking to.

cards.title: Ad 1: Robbi – Nie wieder putzen!
cards.lead: Now that you have the words, we read our first real ad. TechnoMax wants to sell Robbi, and the ad makes big promises. Look at what it says and what it does not say.
cards.body: The TechnoMax ad is bright orange and very loud. Its slogan is Nie wieder putzen! It promises a lot: Robbi cleans the whole flat, he is so quiet that you hear nothing, and the price is only good this week. Ben knows the truth: Robbi was loud and broke after a month. The ad exaggerates.
steps: Slogan: „Robbi – Nie wieder putzen!“
Promise 1: Robbi saugt Ihre ganze Wohnung.
Promise 2: Er ist so leise, dass Sie nichts hören.
Offer: Nur diese Woche: 299 Euro!
Reality (Ben): Robbi war laut, und der Akku war schnell leer.

examples.de: Die Anzeige verspricht viel, deshalb kaufen viele Leute Robbi.
examples.en: The ad promises a lot, so many people buy Robbi.

examples.de: Robbi ist angeblich so leise, dass man nichts hört.
examples.en: Robbi is supposedly so quiet that you hear nothing.

examples.de: Die Werbung übertreibt, finde ich.
examples.en: The advertising exaggerates, I think.

deeper.text: Notice the word angeblich (supposedly). It is how Germans show doubt about a claim without calling it a lie: Robbi ist angeblich leise means 'they say so, but I am not sure'. Ads also love the word nie and the exclamation mark, because short, absolute sentences are easy to remember. A real ad in Germany may not make false claims, so many ads promise feelings, not facts.

example.de: Der Akku hält angeblich zwei Stunden.
example.en: The battery supposedly lasts two hours.

cards.more: Read the ad like a detective. First find the slogan: it is the shortest and loudest line, Nie wieder putzen! Then find the promises: what does Robbi do for you? Then find the pressure: Nur diese Woche wants you to buy now, without thinking. Last, compare it with what you know from Ben's story. Robbi was loud, he hit the walls, the battery died. So the ad exaggerates: it says more than the product can do. That is the key verb today, übertreiben.

cards.title: Ad 2: Anna's poster – Reparieren statt wegwerfen
cards.lead: After the loud TechnoMax ad we look at a very different one. Anna makes a poster for the Repair-Café, and it sells no product at all. It wants people to change their habits.
cards.body: Anna's poster is green and simple. It shows a photo of real helpers in the Gemeindehaus. The slogan is Reparieren statt wegwerfen (statt = instead of; only learn the slogan). The text is short and honest: when, where, and that it costs nothing. Anna's Zielgruppe are the neighbours in the Kiez. It appeals to people who care about the environment.

rows: echte Helferinnen und Helfer im Gemeindehaus
jeden ersten Samstag, 14 bis 17 Uhr, kostenlos

examples.de: Das Plakat spricht Leute an, die nachhaltig leben möchten.
examples.en: The poster appeals to people who want to live sustainably.

examples.de: Die Botschaft des Plakats ist klar.
examples.en: The message of the poster is clear.

examples.de: Die echten Fotos fallen sofort auf.
examples.en: The real photos stand out at once.

deeper.text: Two separable verbs help you describe any ad. ansprechen takes a person in the accusative: Das Plakat spricht mich an (it appeals to me). auffallen takes a person in the dative: Das Plakat fällt mir auf (I notice it). The thing that stands out is the subject, not you. In the Perfekt auffallen uses sein: Das Plakat ist mir sofort aufgefallen.

example.de: Das Plakat ist mir sofort aufgefallen.
example.en: I noticed the poster at once.

cards.more: Imagine you walk past both ads on the same wall. The orange TechnoMax ad shouts at you and wants your money today. Anna's green poster speaks quietly and wants something else: that you bring your broken toaster instead of buying a new one. So an ad does not always sell a product. Sometimes it sells an idea, die Botschaft. Ask three questions about every ad: Who is it for? What does it want me to do? Do I believe it?

cards.title: Comparing the two ads
cards.lead: You have seen both ads. Now we put them side by side with a tool you already know, the comparative with als, and with am besten for the one you like most.
cards.body: Compare with adjective + -er + als: Die Anzeige ist bunter als das Plakat. Short adjectives often add an umlaut: laut → lauter, but groß → größer. For the winner use am + -sten: Am besten gefällt mir das Plakat. Useful adjectives for ads: bunt, laut, ehrlich, persönlich, glaubwürdig, auffällig, überzeugend.

rows: Am besten gefällt mir das Plakat.

examples.de: Die Anzeige ist auffälliger als das Plakat.
examples.en: The ad is more eye-catching than the poster.

examples.de: Das Plakat ist glaubwürdiger, weil es echte Fotos zeigt.
examples.en: The poster is more credible because it shows real photos.

examples.de: Am besten gefällt mir Annas Slogan.
examples.en: I like Anna's slogan best.

deeper.text: Long adjectives do not change: ehrlich → ehrlicher, glaubwürdig → glaubwürdiger, never 'mehr glaubwürdig'. German has no 'more + adjective' like English. To say the two ads are equal, use so … wie: Das Plakat ist so bunt wie die Anzeige. With nicht so … wie you make a polite negative comparison: Die Anzeige ist nicht so ehrlich wie das Plakat.

example.de: Die Anzeige ist nicht so ehrlich wie das Plakat.
example.en: The ad is not as honest as the poster.

cards.more: Use a simple trick: one adjective, two ads, one als. Pick a word from the list, for example ehrlich. Add -er: ehrlicher. Then decide which ad has more of it and put that ad first: Das Plakat ist ehrlicher als die Anzeige. Do the same with bunt, laut and auffällig, and you already have four sentences for a comparison. To finish, choose your favourite with am besten gefällt mir. The thing you like is the subject, and mir stays in the dative.

cards.title: Giving your opinion
cards.lead: A comparison only describes. Now we add your own voice, with opinion phrases you met in A2 and two new ones, and we watch where the verb goes after each phrase.
cards.body: Meiner Meinung nach fills position 1, so the verb comes next: Meiner Meinung nach ist die Anzeige übertrieben. After Ich finde, dass … the verb goes to the end. Mich überzeugt …, weil … names what convinces you. With deshalb you give the result: Die Werbung verspricht viel, deshalb glaube ich ihr nicht.
steps: Meiner Meinung nach + VERB + subject …: Meiner Meinung nach ist das Plakat besser.
Ich finde, dass … VERB.: Ich finde, dass die Anzeige übertreibt.
Mich überzeugt …, weil … VERB.: Mich überzeugt das Plakat, weil es ehrlich ist.
… , deshalb + VERB + subject: Die Werbung ist laut, deshalb nervt sie mich.

examples.de: Meiner Meinung nach ist die Anzeige nicht glaubwürdig.
examples.en: In my opinion the ad is not credible.

examples.de: Ich finde, dass das Plakat ehrlicher ist.
examples.en: I think that the poster is more honest.

examples.de: Die Anzeige übertreibt, deshalb kaufe ich Robbi nicht.
examples.en: The ad exaggerates, so I am not buying Robbi.

deeper.text: At B1 you can sound more formal with Ich bin der Meinung, dass …, which is common in essays and discussions. In speaking, Germans also say Für mich ist … or Ich halte das für übertrieben (halten für = to consider). Be careful with ich meine: it means 'I think', not 'I mean' in the sense of 'I intend'. Mix two phrases in one answer so you do not repeat yourself.

example.de: Ich bin der Meinung, dass die Anzeige übertreibt.
example.en: I am of the opinion that the ad exaggerates.

cards.more: Picture each phrase as a door that decides where the verb sits. Meiner Meinung nach is a heavy door in position 1: after it, the verb walks in first and the subject follows. dass is a door to a side room: the verb goes all the way to the back wall. deshalb works like Meiner Meinung nach, the verb comes straight after it. If you are unsure in a test, say the sentence slowly and ask: which door did I open? Then you know the verb's place.

cards.title: Ben and Anna disagree
cards.lead: Now everything comes together in a short talk. Ben and Anna look at both ads in the WG kitchen and do not agree. Listen for the comparisons, the opinion phrases and the verb positions.
cards.body: Ben still likes the TechnoMax ad: it stands out and it is funny. Anna finds it exaggerated and prefers her honest poster. Both give reasons. Notice how they disagree politely: Das stimmt, aber … and Da hast du recht, trotzdem … At the end they find a small compromise.
steps: Ben: Die Anzeige von TechnoMax fällt sofort auf. Sie ist bunter als dein Plakat.
Anna: Das stimmt, aber meiner Meinung nach übertreibt sie total.
Ben: Na ja, Robbi war wirklich nicht so leise, wie die Anzeige verspricht.
Anna: Siehst du? Mein Plakat ist ehrlicher, deshalb ist es glaubwürdiger.
Ben: Da hast du recht. Trotzdem ist dein Plakat ein bisschen langweilig.
Anna: Okay, dann mache ich die Farbe heller, sodass es mehr auffällt.

examples.de: Das stimmt, aber meiner Meinung nach übertreibt sie total.
examples.en: That's true, but in my opinion it exaggerates completely.

examples.de: Mein Plakat ist ehrlicher, deshalb ist es glaubwürdiger.
examples.en: My poster is more honest, so it is more credible.

examples.de: Ich mache die Farbe heller, sodass es mehr auffällt.
examples.en: I'll make the colour brighter so that it stands out more.

deeper.text: Look at line 2: after aber, meiner Meinung nach still fills position 1, so the verb follows it. aber itself takes no position, it stands outside the clause, like und and oder. Also notice that auffallen joins up again at the end of a sodass clause: es fällt auf becomes …, sodass es auffällt. Every separable verb does this in a subordinate clause.

example.de: Das Plakat ist grün, aber meiner Meinung nach fällt es auf.
example.en: The poster is green, but in my opinion it stands out.

cards.more: Listen to the shape of this talk, not only the words. Each person first accepts something the other said: Das stimmt, Da hast du recht. Then comes the turn: aber or trotzdem. Then comes their own point with a reason. This pattern of yes, but, because is how Germans disagree without a fight, at home and at work. Try it yourself with a friend's opinion about any ad: agree with one small part first, and only then say what you think differently.

lessons.title: Wie funktioniert Werbung?: strategies and taking notes (Stichpunkte)
lessons.goal: Understand how advertising works (feelings, humour, offers, repetition …), take short notes in Stichpunkte while reading or listening, turn notes back into sentences, and plan ads for Herr Ali with lassen, wegen and trotz.

grammar.topic: Review: lassen + infinitive at the end; wegen and trotz + genitive in short statements
grammar.point: lassen means someone else does the job: Herr Ali lässt Flyer drucken. lassen is the verb in position 2, the second verb goes to the end, and there is never zu. wegen + genitive gives a reason, trotz + genitive a contrast: wegen der Kosten, trotz des Preises. In Stichpunkte you can keep just the noun phrase.
grammar.oneLine: Wegen der Kosten lässt Herr Ali nur 500 Flyer drucken.

mistake.wrong: Herr Ali lässt die Flyer zu drucken.
mistake.right: Herr Ali lässt die Flyer drucken.
mistake.why: After lassen the infinitive stands at the end without zu, like after a modal verb.

terms.meaning: notes in key words, not full sentences: Flyer → billig, aber viel Papier
a plan for how to reach a goal; in ads: how to make people notice and buy
have something done by someone else: Er lässt Flyer drucken.

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Die Werbung ist bunt' to 'Warum wirkt sie?'
cards.body: In the last lesson you described ads: bunt, laut, ehrlich. Today we ask a deeper question: why does an ad work? You learn the main tricks of advertising and a study skill for B1, taking notes in Stichpunkte. Herr Ali needs both, because he wants new guests for his restaurant „Zum Löwen“.
steps: You already know: Die Anzeige ist bunter als das Plakat. Ben lässt Robbi reparieren.
New today: words for ad strategies and how to write good Stichpunkte.
By the end you can: explain how an ad works, take notes on a short talk and plan ads for Herr Ali.

examples.de: Die Anzeige von TechnoMax ist sehr bunt.
examples.en: The TechnoMax ad is very colourful.
examples.why: You know this: describing an ad.

examples.de: Die Anzeige wirkt, weil sie Gefühle zeigt.
examples.en: The ad works because it shows feelings.
examples.why: New today: asking why an ad works.

cards.more: Think of a song from an ad that you cannot get out of your head, or a funny commercial that you told a friend about. Neither of them happened by chance. People planned every second of them so that you remember the product. Today you look behind the ad, like a mechanic who opens a machine. And because Mira hears about this in a university seminar, you also learn how to write down the important points fast, without writing every word.

cards.title: How ads work: strategies
cards.lead: We start with the toolbox. Every ad uses one or more strategies to catch your attention and change what you do. Once you know their names, you can see them everywhere.
cards.body: Ads use a few strategies again and again. They show feelings, like Glück or Familie. They make you laugh with Humor. They use bekannte Personen, for example a famous footballer. They give an Angebot or a Rabatt. They make you afraid of a problem. And they use Wiederholung and Musik, so that you remember the product.

rows: Ohne Robbi ist Ihre Wohnung schmutzig.

examples.de: Die Werbung für Blitz-Limo arbeitet mit Humor.
examples.en: The ad for Blitz-Limo works with humour.

examples.de: Wegen der Wiederholung kennt jeder den Slogan.
examples.en: Because of the repetition everyone knows the slogan.

examples.de: Gefühle haben oft eine starke Wirkung.
examples.en: Feelings often have a strong effect.

deeper.text: Two verbs describe what ads do. beeinflussen means to influence: Werbung beeinflusst uns, often without our noticing it. werben für means to advertise for something: TechnoMax wirbt für Robbi. werben changes its vowel like helfen: er hilft, er wirbt; Perfekt, hat geworben. And wirken (to have an effect) gives the noun die Wirkung.

example.de: TechnoMax wirbt mit Humor für Robbi.
example.en: TechnoMax advertises Robbi with humour.

cards.more: Ask yourself one question about any ad: what does it want me to feel? A family at breakfast wants you to feel warm and safe. A dog chasing Robbi wants you to laugh, and people share funny clips. A famous singer wants you to think: if she drinks it, it must be good. A big red 20 Prozent wants you to feel that you will lose money if you wait. Every strategy is simply a different feeling that leads you to the product.

cards.title: Herr Ali's question: Flyer oder Social Media?
cards.lead: Now we use the strategies for a real case. Herr Ali wants more guests for „Zum Löwen“, and he and Leon discuss how to advertise. Watch how lassen comes back.
cards.body: Herr Ali is old-school: he wants paper flyers. He does not print them himself, he lässt sie in einer Druckerei drucken. Leon, who helps in his kitchen on Saturdays, thinks social media has more Reichweite. Herr Ali is not sure, but he lässt Leon ein Video für Instagram machen. Wegen der Kosten they start small: 500 flyers and one video.

rows: Er lässt Leon ein Video machen.

examples.de: Herr Ali lässt 500 Flyer drucken.
examples.en: Herr Ali is having 500 flyers printed.

examples.de: Er lässt Leon ein Video für Instagram machen.
examples.en: He lets Leon make a video for Instagram.

examples.de: Trotz der Kosten möchte Herr Ali Flyer haben.
examples.en: Despite the costs Herr Ali wants flyers.

deeper.text: Look again at the two lassen sentences. In the first, lassen means 'have done': the Druckerei prints, Herr Ali pays. In the second it means 'allow': Leon wants to make the video and Herr Ali lets him. The grammar is the same. Only the context tells you who wants the action. die Kundschaft is a useful word here: it means all the customers of a shop, singular only.

example.de: Die Kundschaft von Herrn Ali kommt gern wieder.
example.en: Herr Ali's customers like coming back.

cards.more: Picture two ways to reach people. A flyer is like a letter: you hold it, you put it on the fridge, but it only reaches the street where you leave it. A post on Instagram is like shouting in a big square: many people hear it, but they forget it quickly. Herr Ali chooses both, but he does neither job alone. The printing company prints, Leon films. That is why lassen appears twice: Herr Ali is the boss who organises, not the person who works.

cards.title: Taking notes in Stichpunkte
cards.lead: Herr Ali and Leon talk fast, and Mira has a whole seminar about advertising. To keep the main points, you need a study skill: writing Stichpunkte instead of full sentences.
cards.body: Stichpunkte are short notes. Write only key words: nouns, adjectives and verbs in the infinitive. Leave out articles and small words. Use symbols: → for a result, + for an advantage, – for a disadvantage, ? for an open question. One line = one idea. This way you can write while you listen.
steps: Text: „Flyer sind billig, aber man braucht viel Papier. Social Media hat eine große Reichweite.“
Step 1: find the key words: Flyer, billig, Papier, Social Media, Reichweite, groß.
Step 2: drop articles and small words: no die, der, man, aber.
Step 3: use symbols: Flyer: + billig, – viel Papier
Step 4: one line per idea: Social Media: + große Reichweite

examples.de: Flyer: billig, aber viel Papier
examples.en: Flyers: cheap, but a lot of paper

examples.de: Humor → Kundschaft teilt Video
examples.en: humour → customers share video

examples.de: Wiederholung + Musik → Slogan merken
examples.en: repetition + music → remember slogan

deeper.text: Germans often use a few standard short forms in notes: z. B. (zum Beispiel), usw. (und so weiter), ca. (circa, about) and bzw. (beziehungsweise, or rather). You will see them in the B1 exam too. In the exam you may take notes during the listening, and only your final answers count. So Stichpunkte are for you, they do not need to be correct sentences, but the key nouns must be right.

example.de: Strategien: z. B. Humor, Gefühle usw.
example.en: strategies: e.g. humour, feelings etc.

cards.more: Imagine you send a text message that costs one euro per word. You would never write 'Die Flyer sind leider sehr teuer.' You would write 'Flyer – teuer'. That is exactly how Stichpunkte work. Ask for every word: do I need it to remember the idea tomorrow? Articles, man, und and ist almost never pass this test. Nouns and numbers almost always do. Symbols save even more: an arrow says 'so, therefore' with one stroke of the pen.

cards.title: From notes back to sentences
cards.lead: Notes are only half the job. Later you must speak or write about what you heard, so we practise the way back: from Stichpunkte to full, correct German sentences.
cards.body: To turn notes into sentences, add what you left out: the article, a verb in the right form and a connector. A minus often becomes aber, an arrow becomes deshalb or sodass, a plus becomes und or außerdem. Check the verb position: deshalb takes the verb next, sodass sends it to the end.
steps: Note: Flyer: + billig, – viel Papier → Flyer sind billig, aber man braucht viel Papier.
Note: Social Media → große Reichweite → Social Media hat eine große Reichweite.
Note: Humor → Leute teilen Video → Das Video ist lustig, deshalb teilen es viele Leute.
Note: wegen Kosten: nur 500 Flyer → Wegen der Kosten lässt Herr Ali nur 500 Flyer drucken.

examples.de: Flyer sind billig, aber man braucht viel Papier.
examples.en: Flyers are cheap, but you need a lot of paper.

examples.de: Das Video ist lustig, deshalb teilen es viele Leute.
examples.en: The video is funny, so lots of people share it.

examples.de: Wegen der Kosten lässt Herr Ali nur 500 Flyer drucken.
examples.en: Because of the costs Herr Ali is only having 500 flyers printed.

deeper.text: In notes, wegen and trotz are perfect because they need only a noun: wegen Kosten, trotz Regen. In a full written sentence add the article in the genitive: wegen der Kosten, trotz des Regens. Some short forms without an article are also fine in normal German, for example trotz Regen. But in the exam and in letters, write the full genitive.

example.de: Trotz des Regens verteilt Leon die Flyer.
example.en: Despite the rain Leon hands out the flyers.

cards.more: Think of notes as a dried meal and sentences as the cooked dish. To cook it, you add water and salt: in German that is the article, the right verb form and the little connecting words. Each symbol already tells you which connector to use. The minus is a warning, so take aber. The arrow is a result, so take deshalb or sodass. Then read your sentence once and check only one thing: is the verb in the right place?

cards.title: Mira's seminar: a short talk on advertising
cards.lead: Now we test both skills on a real text. Mira gives a short talk in her university seminar. First read it, then compare your notes with Mira's own Stichpunkte below.
cards.body: Mira gives a 90-word talk in her seminar. Read it step by step, as if you heard it, and write your own Stichpunkte. Then compare them with Mira's notes in the table: key words, numbers for the points and one line for her tip.
steps: „Warum kaufen wir Produkte aus der Werbung? Werbung arbeitet oft mit Gefühlen. Eine glückliche Familie macht uns froh, und wir verbinden dieses Gefühl mit dem Produkt.
Wichtig ist auch die Wiederholung: Wir sehen denselben Slogan zehnmal, deshalb merken wir ihn.
Humor funktioniert besonders gut im Internet, weil Leute lustige Videos teilen. Rabatte machen Druck: Nur heute!
Trotz dieser Tricks können wir kritisch bleiben. Fragen Sie sich: Brauche ich das wirklich? Meiner Meinung nach ist das die beste Strategie gegen Werbung.“

examples.de: Wir sehen denselben Slogan zehnmal, deshalb merken wir ihn.
examples.en: We see the same slogan ten times, so we remember it.

examples.de: Humor funktioniert gut, weil Leute lustige Videos teilen.
examples.en: Humour works well because people share funny videos.

examples.de: Trotz dieser Tricks können wir kritisch bleiben.
examples.en: Despite these tricks we can stay critical.

deeper.text: Good notes follow the structure of the talk. Mira gives signals: Wichtig ist auch … starts a new point, Meiner Meinung nach … starts her opinion. Listen for such signal words and start a new line each time. Numbers 1, 2, 3 for the points and a separate line for the speaker's opinion make your notes easy to use later. dieser Tricks is a plural genitive with dies-: like der, no extra ending on the noun.

example.de: Wichtig ist auch die Musik.
example.en: The music is also important.

cards.more: Compare the talk and the notes line by line. Ninety words became about twenty. Mira kept the four strategies, one short reason for each and her final tip. She threw away everything you can rebuild later: wir, uns, dieses, besonders. Notice also the order: the notes follow the talk from top to bottom, so you can retell it in the same order. If you can say Mira's talk again from her six lines, your notes are good enough.

cards.title: Your strategy for „Zum Löwen“
cards.lead: To finish, you become the advertising expert. Herr Ali asks you for a plan. Use the strategies, write your plan in Stichpunkte and then explain it in full sentences.
cards.body: Herr Ali's goal: more guests on weekdays. Choose two strategies and one medium: Flyer, Plakat or Social Media. Write your plan in Stichpunkte, then explain it in three or four sentences with lassen and wegen or trotz. Look at the model below and then write your own.
steps: Ziel: mehr Gäste, Montag bis Donnerstag
Strategie 1: Angebot → Mittagsmenü 9,90 €
Strategie 2: Gefühle → Fotos: Familie am Tisch
Medium: Flyer (Kiez) + Instagram (junge Leute)
Sätze: Herr Ali lässt Flyer mit einem Angebot drucken. Wegen der Reichweite macht Leon auch Fotos für Instagram.

examples.de: Herr Ali lässt Flyer mit einem Mittagsmenü drucken.
examples.en: Herr Ali has flyers with a lunch menu printed.

examples.de: Wegen der Reichweite macht Leon Fotos für Instagram.
examples.en: Because of the reach Leon takes photos for Instagram.

examples.de: Die Fotos zeigen Familien, sodass die Kundschaft Lust bekommt.
examples.en: The photos show families, so that customers feel like coming.

deeper.text: When you advise someone, German often uses the Konjunktiv II forms you know from A2: Sie könnten Flyer drucken lassen. Sie sollten auch Social Media ausprobieren. They sound more polite than the imperative. Notice the order with lassen and a modal verb: the modal is in position 2, and drucken lassen stands at the end as a pair, with lassen last.

example.de: Sie könnten Flyer drucken lassen.
example.en: You could have flyers printed.

cards.more: Do the task like a real advertising agency in three short moves. First the goal in one line: what should change for Herr Ali? Then the tools: one or two strategies and one place where people will see the ad. Only then the words: the sentences you would say to Herr Ali in a meeting. Agencies always plan from goal to tools to text, never the other way round, because a beautiful slogan is useless if it reaches the wrong people.

lessons.title: Bitte keine Werbung!: advertising in Germany + chapter review
lessons.goal: Talk about advertising in Germany and in your own country, and use all the chapter grammar together in one text: lassen, deshalb/darum/daher/sodass, the genitive, wegen, trotz and trotzdem.

grammar.topic: Chapter review: lassen, consequences (deshalb, sodass), genitive, wegen/trotz/trotzdem
grammar.point: No new grammar today. Reason: weil + clause, deshalb + verb next, wegen + genitive. Contrast: obwohl + clause, trotzdem + verb next, trotz + genitive. Result: …, sodass … verb at the end. lassen + infinitive at the end: someone else does it. Genitive: des …(e)s for der/das, der for die and plural.
grammar.oneLine: Wegen der Werbeflut hat Mira einen Aufkleber am Briefkasten, deshalb bekommt sie keine Flyer.

mistake.wrong: Wegen des Werbung kaufen viele Leute mehr.
mistake.right: Wegen der Werbung kaufen viele Leute mehr.
mistake.why: die Werbung is feminine: the genitive article is der, and the noun gets no ending.

terms.meaning: public broadcasting, paid for by a fee from all households: ARD and ZDF
one table that shows the same idea (reason, contrast) with a clause, a position-1 word and a noun
a short text with your opinion, reasons, a counter-argument and a conclusion

cards.title: Before we start: everything from this chapter in one text
cards.body: This is the last lesson of Das ist ja praktisch! You learn two real facts about advertising in Germany, and you compare them with your own country. Then you put the whole chapter together: lassen, deshalb and sodass, the genitive, wegen and trotz. At the end you write a short comment about advertising.
steps: You already know: Herr Ali lässt Flyer drucken. Wegen der Kosten druckt er nur 500.
New today: the „Bitte keine Werbung“ sticker, the ARD/ZDF rule and words for consumers.
By the end you can: compare advertising in two countries and write a comment with all the chapter grammar.

examples.de: Wegen der Kosten lässt Herr Ali nur 500 Flyer drucken.
examples.en: Because of the costs Herr Ali is only having 500 flyers printed.
examples.why: You know this: wegen and lassen from this chapter.

examples.de: Mira möchte keine Flyer, deshalb hat sie einen Aufkleber am Briefkasten.
examples.en: Mira does not want flyers, so she has a sticker on her letterbox.
examples.why: New today: the sticker on German letterboxes.

cards.more: Walk through a German apartment building and look at the letterboxes by the front door. On many of them you will see the same small sticker. It tells you something about how Germans feel about advertising: many like it in its place, but not in their private space. Today you learn this and one more rule from German TV, and then you use everything from the chapter at once, like the last level of a game where all the old tools come back.

cards.title: Advertising in Germany: two facts
cards.lead: We start with culture. Germany has a few clear habits and rules about advertising. Two of them you will meet in daily life very soon: one at your letterbox and one on TV.
cards.body: Many German letterboxes have a sticker: „Bitte keine Werbung“. Then nobody should put flyers or other advertising inside. Letters still arrive. On TV, the public channels ARD and ZDF are öffentlich-rechtlich: they show no advertising after 20 Uhr and none on Sundays and public holidays. Private channels show many Werbepausen.

rows: Aufkleber „Bitte keine Werbung“ → keine Flyer, keine Prospekte
keine Werbung an Sonn- und Feiertagen

examples.de: Wegen des Aufklebers bekommt Mira keine Flyer.
examples.en: Because of the sticker Mira gets no flyers.

examples.de: Nach 20 Uhr zeigt das ZDF keine Werbung.
examples.en: After 8 p.m. ZDF shows no advertising.

examples.de: Am Sonntag gibt es in der ARD keine Werbepause.
examples.en: On Sunday there is no commercial break on ARD.

deeper.text: Why no evening ads? ARD and ZDF are paid for mainly by a fee that every household pays, the Rundfunkbeitrag, so they need much less money from advertising. Private channels like RTL live from advertising, so they have more Werbepausen. Notice the articles: die ARD (feminine) but das ZDF (neuter). In speaking, many people just say im Ersten for ARD and im Zweiten for ZDF.

example.de: Den Film zeigen sie heute Abend im Ersten.
example.en: They are showing the film on ARD tonight.

cards.more: Imagine two doors. The first is the door of your home: the sticker on the letterbox is like a sign saying 'no salespeople, please'. The postman still brings your letters, only the advertising stays outside. The second door is the TV in the evening: when you watch the news or a film on ARD or ZDF after eight, nobody interrupts it with ads, and on Sundays or holidays not at all. Both rules protect private time from advertising.

cards.title: Here and in your country
cards.lead: Facts become interesting when you compare them. Now you talk about advertising in your own country next to Germany, with the comparatives from lesson 13 and phrases for two places.
cards.body: To compare two countries, say where first: Bei uns …, In Deutschland …, In meinem Land … Then use mehr, weniger or anders: Bei uns gibt es mehr Werbung im Fernsehen. To show a contrast, use aber, or trotzdem with the verb next. Give a reason with weil or wegen.
steps: Bei uns gibt es mehr / weniger Werbung als in Deutschland.
In Deutschland ist die Werbung im Briefkasten anders: viele haben einen Aufkleber.
Bei uns gibt es keine Regel für das Fernsehen, deshalb kommen oft Werbepausen.
Wegen der Werbeflut im Internet nutze ich einen Werbeblocker.

examples.de: Bei uns gibt es mehr Werbung im Fernsehen als in Deutschland.
examples.en: In my country there are more TV ads than in Germany.

examples.de: In meinem Land gibt es keine Aufkleber, trotzdem bekommen wir wenige Flyer.
examples.en: In my country there are no stickers, but we still get few flyers.

examples.de: In Deutschland ist das Abendprogramm ruhiger, weil ARD und ZDF keine Werbung zeigen.
examples.en: In Germany the evening programme is calmer because ARD and ZDF show no ads.

deeper.text: Watch the small words. mehr and weniger never change: mehr Werbung, weniger Flyer. But viel and wenig take endings before a plural noun: viele Flyer, wenige Werbepausen. Also, bei uns means 'in my country' or 'at our home', depending on context, which is very handy in conversation. To be fair in a comparison, add a limiting phrase: soviel ich weiß (as far as I know).

example.de: Soviel ich weiß, gibt es bei uns weniger Werbepausen.
example.en: As far as I know, we have fewer commercial breaks in my country.

cards.more: Think of a simple scale with Germany on one side and your country on the other. For each place where ads appear, ask: more, less or different? Letterbox: are there stickers at home, or do flyers come anyway? TV: are there ads in the evening film? Internet: do you see more ads on your phone than on TV? Say one sentence for each place, starting with the place: Bei uns …, In Deutschland … That order makes your answer clear and easy to follow.

cards.title: Review map: reason, contrast, result
cards.lead: Now the grammar. This chapter gave you many words that say the same idea in different shapes. One map shows them all together, so you can choose the right one quickly.
cards.body: Each idea has three shapes. A conjunction opens a clause with the verb at the end. A word in position 1 is followed directly by the verb. A preposition just needs a noun in the genitive. Reason: weil, deshalb, wegen. Contrast: obwohl, trotzdem, trotz. Result: sodass, with the verb at the end.

examples.de: Weil die Werbung nervt, hat Mira einen Aufkleber.
examples.en: Because the advertising is annoying, Mira has a sticker.

examples.de: Die Werbung nervt, deshalb hat Mira einen Aufkleber.
examples.en: The advertising is annoying, so Mira has a sticker.

examples.de: Trotz des Preises kauft Ben den neuen Akku.
examples.en: Despite the price Ben buys the new battery.

deeper.text: The most common mix-up is trotz and trotzdem. trotz needs a noun right after it: trotz des Regens. trotzdem stands alone and refers back to the sentence before: Es regnet. Trotzdem gehen wir. A quick test: if a noun follows, it is trotz; if a verb follows, it is trotzdem. The same test separates wegen (noun) and deshalb (verb).

example.de: Es regnet. Trotzdem verteilt Leon die Flyer.
example.en: It is raining. Leon hands out the flyers anyway.

cards.more: Read the table like a city map with three streets. On the first street the verb walks to the end: weil, obwohl, sodass. On the second street the verb jumps straight after the word: deshalb, trotzdem. On the third street there is no verb at all, only a noun in the genitive: wegen der Werbung, trotz des Preises. When you write, first decide the idea, reason or contrast, and then choose the street that fits your sentence best.

cards.title: Anna's flyer: lassen and the genitive
cards.lead: Next we see the grammar in a real text. Anna writes a flyer for the Repair-Café, and in a few lines she uses lassen, the genitive and both prepositions of the chapter.
cards.body: Anna's flyer speaks to the reader with Sie. Lassen Sie … is a polite invitation: let us repair it for you. The genitive tells you whose things: die Lampe Ihrer Oma. wegen and trotz give short, strong reasons. Read the flyer and find each structure.
steps: Ihr Toaster ist kaputt? Werfen Sie ihn nicht weg!
Lassen Sie Ihre Geräte im Repair-Café reparieren!
Wir reparieren auch die Lampe Ihrer Oma und das Fahrrad Ihres Sohnes.
Kommen Sie trotz des Regens: Im Gemeindehaus ist es warm.
Wegen der Umwelt: Reparieren statt wegwerfen!

examples.de: Lassen Sie Ihre Geräte im Repair-Café reparieren!
examples.en: Have your devices repaired at the Repair-Café!

examples.de: Wir reparieren auch die Lampe Ihrer Oma.
examples.en: We also repair your grandma's lamp.

examples.de: Kommen Sie trotz des Regens!
examples.en: Come despite the rain!

deeper.text: The Sie-imperative and the question look almost the same: Lassen Sie Ihre Geräte reparieren! and Lassen Sie Ihre Geräte reparieren? Only the punctuation and your voice show the difference. Flyers love the imperative because it sounds direct. With friends you would write Lass dein Fahrrad reparieren! For a group: Lasst eure Geräte reparieren! Use the form that fits your Zielgruppe.

example.de: Lass dein Fahrrad im Repair-Café reparieren!
example.en: Get your bike repaired at the Repair-Café!

cards.more: Imagine you are the reader holding Anna's flyer at the bus stop. Line one asks you a question about your own toaster, so you feel spoken to. Line two tells you what to do, with lassen: you do not need to repair it yourself. Line three uses the genitive to make it personal, your grandma, your son. Lines four and five remove your excuses: the rain, and the reason why it matters. Good advertising grammar is short, polite and speaks directly to you.

cards.title: The story of Robbi: the whole chapter
cards.lead: Before the writing task, we retell the chapter story once in eight sentences. Each sentence uses one structure you learned, so the story is also a grammar review.
cards.body: Read the story of Robbi from the TechnoMax ad to the Repair-Café. Each line has one structure from this chapter: lassen, deshalb, sodass, a genitive, wegen, trotz or trotzdem. Try to tell the story again yourself, first with the text, then without it.
steps: 1. Wegen der Werbung hat Ben Robbi bei TechnoMax bestellt.
2. Die Anzeige hat viel versprochen, deshalb war Ben sehr froh.
3. Aber Robbi war so laut, dass Ben nicht schlafen konnte.
4. Nach einem Monat war der Akku des Roboters immer schnell leer.
5. Ben hat reklamiert, trotzdem wollte TechnoMax 80 Euro für die Reparatur.
6. Ben hat Robbi im Repair-Café reparieren lassen.
7. Trotz des Regens sind viele Nachbarn ins Gemeindehaus gekommen.
8. Jetzt läuft Robbi wieder, sodass Ben nie wieder putzen muss – fast.

examples.de: Wegen der Werbung hat Ben Robbi bei TechnoMax bestellt.
examples.en: Because of the advertising Ben ordered Robbi from TechnoMax.

examples.de: Ben hat Robbi im Repair-Café reparieren lassen.
examples.en: Ben had Robbi repaired at the Repair-Café.

examples.de: Nach einem Monat war der Akku des Roboters immer schnell leer.
examples.en: After a month the robot's battery was always empty quickly.

deeper.text: Look at sentence 6: in the Perfekt, lassen with a second verb does not become gelassen. It stays lassen: Ben hat Robbi reparieren lassen, two infinitives at the end. Only when lassen stands alone do you use gelassen: Ich habe das Handy zu Hause gelassen. This 'double infinitive' also happens with modal verbs, so it may look familiar: Ich habe nicht schlafen können.

example.de: Ich habe mein Handy zu Hause gelassen.
example.en: I left my phone at home.

cards.more: Use the story as a test for your memory, not only your grammar. Cover the text and look only at the numbers. For each number, try to remember what happened: the ad, the joy, the noise, the battery, the complaint, the Repair-Café, the rain, the happy end. Then say the sentence and check it. If you can tell all eight lines with the right connector, you have the whole chapter in your head, ready for the practice day.

cards.title: Writing a comment about advertising
cards.lead: Finally you write. A short comment is a typical B1 task, and you already know its four steps from lesson 12. Now you use them for advertising, with the grammar of the chapter.
cards.body: A comment has four steps: your opinion, a reason, a counter-argument and a conclusion. Use deshalb or wegen for the reason, trotzdem or trotz for the counter-argument. Read the model comment (about 90 words), then write your own with at least one wegen or trotz.
steps: Meinung: Werbung nervt mich oft. Meiner Meinung nach gibt es zu viel davon.
Grund: Wegen der Werbeflut im Internet kann ich mich kaum auf ein Video konzentrieren. Deshalb habe ich einen Werbeblocker.
Gegenargument: Trotzdem ist Werbung manchmal nützlich. Durch einen Flyer habe ich vom Repair-Café erfahren, und dort hat man mein Fahrrad kostenlos repariert.
Fazit: Gezielte, ehrliche Werbung finde ich gut. Aber ich möchte selbst entscheiden, deshalb hat mein Briefkasten jetzt einen Aufkleber: „Bitte keine Werbung“.

examples.de: Wegen der Werbeflut kann ich mich kaum konzentrieren.
examples.en: Because of the flood of ads I can hardly concentrate.

examples.de: Trotzdem ist Werbung manchmal nützlich.
examples.en: Even so, advertising is sometimes useful.

examples.de: Ich möchte selbst entscheiden, deshalb habe ich einen Aufkleber.
examples.en: I want to decide for myself, so I have a sticker.

deeper.text: A strong comment is kritisch but fair: it does not say all advertising is bad. Show both sides and use exact words instead of 'good' and 'bad': manipulieren for unfair tricks, informieren for useful facts, gezielt for ads that reach the right people. A conclusion often starts with Insgesamt … or Zum Schluss … and says what you want, not only what you dislike.

example.de: Insgesamt finde ich ehrliche Werbung nützlich.
example.en: All in all I find honest advertising useful.

cards.more: Build your comment like a sandwich. The top slice is your opinion in one clear sentence. The filling has two layers: first your strongest reason, with wegen or deshalb, then the other side, with trotzdem or trotz, so the reader sees that you are fair. The bottom slice is the conclusion: what you do or want now. Four parts, about ninety words. If one part is missing, the sandwich falls apart, and the examiner notices that first.
